criteria.text: Patients must have histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); cytology alone is not acceptable
Patients must have progressive or recurrent NSCLC
must have failed one and only one prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease
patients must not have received prior gemcitabine chemotherapy
Patients must have measurable disease, as defined by RECIST, within 4 weeks prior to registration
Patients must have an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Bilirubin < 1.5 x upper limit of normal
AST (SGOT) < 3 x upper limit of normal
Serum creatinine =< 1.5 mg/dL, or calculated creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min
Absolute granulocyte count >= 1500/mm3
Hemoglobin >= 9 g/L
Platelet count >= 100,000/mm\^3
Patients must have completed any radiation therapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration
Patients must have completed prior cytotoxic chemotherapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration
have recovered from adverse effects from the chemotherapy to =< Grade 1, or baseline
Patients with brain metastases which have been treated are eligible if the patient is > 3 weeks post completion of treatment for their brain metastases, and patient is neurologically stable
patients with previous brain metastases who have not yet received therapy specifically intended for their brain metastases are not eligible to enroll in this protocol
Life expectancy greater than 3 months
Pregnant women are excluded from this study
breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with Triapine®
a negative serum pregnancy test is required within 14 days of study entry

women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation
HIV-positive patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy are excluded from the study
Patients must not have an active second malignancy

Patients must not have, at the time of registration, uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements
a history of myocardial infarction within the prior 6 months
symptomatic congestive heart failure
unstable angina pectoris
cardiac arrhythmia requiring medical intervention (with the exception of chronic, stable, asymptomatic atrial fibrillation)
pulmonary disease requiring oxygen
Patients must not have dementia or active psychosis
Patients must not have used any investigational agent in the month before study enrollment
Patients must not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to Triapine® or other agents used in this study
Patients must not have a clinical history of G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency
persons at high risk for this condition (patients of African, Asian, or Mediterranean origin/ancestry) must undergo specific clinical testing at protocol entry for this condition
patients testing positive for G6PD deficiency are excluded from protocol entry

transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "A Phase II Trial of Triapine (NSC #663249) in Combination With Gemcitabine as Second Line Treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a biopsy or tissue sample that confirmed your lung cancer is non-small cell (NSCLC)? A diagnosis based only on cells from fluid or sputum isn't enough for this study. If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, a tissue biopsy confirmed my non-small cell lung cancer, not just cells from fluid. I also want to mention that I haven't used any investigational agents recently, I don't have G6PD deficiency, and I would agree to use contraception during the study.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for sharing that. To help us understand your treatment history, has your non-small cell lung cancer gotten worse or come back after your initial treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, unfortunately, the cancer did grow again. The scans showed it coming back after my initial treatment failed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, have you received exactly one prior chemotherapy regimen for your advanced lung cancer, and no more?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I have had exactly one chemotherapy regimen for my advanced cancer, and it failed. The scans showed it growing again.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received gemcitabine chemotherapy before? This is a specific type of chemo used for lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had gemcitabine. I'm happy to provide more details if needed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a scan to check for measurable disease within the last 4 weeks? (Measurable disease means the cancer can be clearly seen and measured on the scan.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the specific timing of my last scan, but I know my scans showed the cancer growing again after my last treatment. I can check with my doctor to confirm the exact date if that helps.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be clear, did you have a scan done within the last 4 weeks that showed the cancer could be measured? It's okay if you're not sure; you can check with your doctor and let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I had a scan done within the last 4 weeks specifically. I know my scans showed the cancer growing, but I don't have the exact dates memorized. I would need to check with my doctor to be certain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know your ECOG performance status? It’s a score from 0 to 4 that measures how well you can do daily activities. 0 means fully active, and 1 means restricted in strenuous activity but able to do light work. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I would say my status is 0 or 1. I walk the dog every morning and do all my own housework, so I'm quite active.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us confirm your status, can you do strenuous activities like heavy lifting or running, or are you limited to light work only?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I can do light work like walking the dog and housework, but I'm not sure if I can do strenuous activities like heavy lifting or running anymore. I tend to be cautious with my energy these days.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you completed any radiation therapy for your cancer? If so, was it at least 3 weeks before you would start this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I finished radiation therapy to my chest two months ago, which is well past the three-week requirement. I also want to mention that my last chemotherapy was six weeks ago, so that's covered too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you recovered from any side effects of your chemotherapy to Grade 1 or your baseline level? Grade 1 means mild symptoms that don't interfere with daily life. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the specific medical grading of my side effects, but I feel well enough to walk the dog and do my housework. I don't have any severe symptoms interfering with my daily life.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you're not sure about the medical grade, could you tell me if you still have any side effects from chemo that are moderate or severe, or are they all mild (Grade 1) or gone?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know the specific medical grades of my side effects, but I feel well enough to walk the dog and do my housework without severe symptoms interfering with my daily life.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with brain metastases? If so, was it treated, and have you been neurologically stable for at least 3 weeks since treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have brain metastases. I haven't been diagnosed with that, but I'm not entirely sure if they checked specifically for it in the recent scans. I would need to check with my doctor to be certain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, have you ever been told by a doctor that you have cancer that has spread to your brain? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been told by a doctor that my cancer has spread to my brain. I am not sure if they checked specifically for it in recent scans, but I have no diagnosis of brain metastases.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for more than 3 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I certainly hope so! I feel quite active and am managing my daily routine well, so I don't see any reason why I wouldn't. I'm optimistic about my future.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be clear, do you expect to live for more than 3 months based on your current health? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I certainly expect to live for more than 3 months. I feel quite active and am managing my daily routine well, so I don't see any reason why I wouldn't.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or do you think you might be pregnant?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not pregnant. I am 66 years old, so that is certainly not a concern for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not breastfeeding. I am 66 years old, so that is certainly not a concern for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a blood pregnancy test within the last 14 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I haven't had a blood pregnancy test recently, and at my age, I don't think it's typically required or done, but I'm not certain about the specific protocol.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently taking medication for HIV, such as combination antiretroviral therapy?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not taking any medication for HIV. I have never been diagnosed with HIV.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides my lung cancer. I've only ever dealt with this one.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any active infections, or any ongoing health or personal issues that might make it hard to follow the study schedule?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any active infections or ongoing issues that would make it hard to follow the schedule. I'm feeling well and ready to participate.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a heart attack (myocardial infarction) in the last 6 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not had a heart attack in the last six months. I feel quite active and healthy otherwise.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with symptomatic congestive heart failure? This means heart failure that causes symptoms like shortness of breath or swelling.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with symptomatic congestive heart failure. I feel quite active and healthy otherwise.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with unstable angina pectoris? This is a type of chest pain that happens at rest or with minimal activity and may signal an increased risk of heart attack.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with unstable angina. I feel quite active and healthy otherwise.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart rhythm problem (cardiac arrhythmia) that required medical treatment? This excludes chronic, stable, and symptom-free atrial fibrillation.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with a heart rhythm problem that required treatment. My heart has always been fine, and I don't have any issues like atrial fibrillation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently use supplemental oxygen for any lung or breathing condition?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not need oxygen for my lungs. I am quite active and manage my breathing well on my own.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with dementia or active psychosis? Dementia involves memory and thinking problems, and psychosis involves losing touch with reality.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with dementia or active psychosis. I am quite clear-headed and have always been able to manage my daily life and work without any issues like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you taken part in any other clinical trials or received any investigational medications in the last month?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not taken part in any other clinical trials or received any investigational medications in the last month. I mentioned earlier that I haven't used any investigational agents recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to Triapine or any other drugs with a similar chemical or biologic makeup?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I came out in a rash once with an antibiotic, but I don't remember which one. I have never had a reaction to Triapine specifically.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, do you know if that antibiotic was similar to Triapine or any other drugs used in this study? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if that antibiotic was similar to Triapine or the other drugs used in this study. I don't remember the name of the antibiotic, so I can't say for certain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been tested for G6PD deficiency, a condition that affects how your body processes certain medications? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I have been tested for G6PD deficiency. They tested me for it years ago and it was fine, so I do not have the condition.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

criteria.text: Patients must have histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); cytology alone is not acceptable
Patients must have progressive or recurrent NSCLC
must have failed one and only one prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease
patients must not have received prior gemcitabine chemotherapy
Patients must have measurable disease, as defined by RECIST, within 4 weeks prior to registration
Patients must have an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1
Bilirubin < 1.5 x upper limit of normal
AST (SGOT) < 3 x upper limit of normal
Serum creatinine =< 1.5 mg/dL, or calculated creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min
Absolute granulocyte count >= 1500/mm3
Hemoglobin >= 9 g/L
Platelet count >= 100,000/mm\^3
Patients must have completed any radiation therapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration
Patients must have completed prior cytotoxic chemotherapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration
have recovered from adverse effects from the chemotherapy to =< Grade 1, or baseline
Patients with brain metastases which have been treated are eligible if the patient is > 3 weeks post completion of treatment for their brain metastases, and patient is neurologically stable
patients with previous brain metastases who have not yet received therapy specifically intended for their brain metastases are not eligible to enroll in this protocol
Life expectancy greater than 3 months
Pregnant women are excluded from this study
breastfeeding should be discontinued if the mother is treated with Triapine®
a negative serum pregnancy test is required within 14 days of study entry

women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation
HIV-positive patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy are excluded from the study
Patients must not have an active second malignancy

Patients must not have, at the time of registration, uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements
a history of myocardial infarction within the prior 6 months
symptomatic congestive heart failure
unstable angina pectoris
cardiac arrhythmia requiring medical intervention (with the exception of chronic, stable, asymptomatic atrial fibrillation)
pulmonary disease requiring oxygen
Patients must not have dementia or active psychosis
Patients must not have used any investigational agent in the month before study enrollment
Patients must not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to Triapine® or other agents used in this study
Patients must not have a clinical history of G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency
persons at high risk for this condition (patients of African, Asian, or Mediterranean origin/ancestry) must undergo specific clinical testing at protocol entry for this condition
patients testing positive for G6PD deficiency are excluded from protocol entry

criteria.text: Males and females >=18 years of age
Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), performed on a biopsy that occurred within the last 90 days.
Documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples by Clinical Laboratory Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-approved test
received no more than 28 days of treatment
no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment adverse events possibly related to treatment with the EGFR TKI
Positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer (mediastinal staging biopsy is allowed but not required)
Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (or CT if contraindication to MRI) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease
Documentation that the patient is a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon
The patient must have a tumor size >=1 centimeter (cm) in its longest diameter.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 0-1

Any unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinumtherapy-related neuropathy is allowed
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =< 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)

Bilirubin =< 1.5 x ULN, (Patients with documented Gilbert's syndrome and conjugated bilirubin within the normal range may be allowed into the study; in this event, it will be documented that the patient was eligible based on conjugated bilirubin levels)
Potassium and magnesium within normal range, patients may receive supplements to meet this requirement
Leukocytes > 3,000/microliter (mcL)
Hemoglobin >= 9 g/dL, with no blood transfusions in the 28 days prior to study entry
Absolute neutrophil count > 1,500/mcL
Platelets > 100,000/mcL
Creatinine Clearance (CrCl) > 50 mL/min for patients with serum creatinine (SCr) > 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)
Ability to swallow oral medications
must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment
agree to use highly effective contraception, during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib
Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP): women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation
Women NOT of childbearing potential: women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal

Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy and/or bilateral salpingectomy but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion; tubal occlusion is considered a highly effective method of birth control but does not absolutely exclude possibility of pregnancy; (the term occlusion refers to both occluding and ligating techniques that do not physically remove the oviducts)
Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP (e.g. undergo pregnancy testing etc., as required by the study protocol)
Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause; the following age-specific requirements apply:

Women under 50 years old will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments and with luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone levels in the postmenopausal range
Women over 50 years of age will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments
Acceptable contraception methods are:
Total sexual abstinence (abstinence must be for the total duration of the trial and the follow-up period)
Vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom (with participant assurance that partner received post-vasectomy confirmation of azoospermia)
Tubal occlusion plus male condom
Intra-uterine device - provided coils are copper-banded, plus male condom
Intra-uterine system (IUS) levonorgestrel IUS (e.g., Mirena), plus male condom
Medroxyprogesterone injections (Depo-Provera) plus male condom
Etonogestrel implants (e.g., Implanon, Norplan) plus male condom
Normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills, plus male condom
Norelgestromin / ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom
Intravaginal device (e.g., ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel) plus male condom
Cerazette (desogestrel) plus male condom (Cerazette is currently the only highly efficacious progesterone based pill)
Unacceptable Contraception Methods The following methods are considered not to be highly effective and are therefore not acceptable contraceptive methods:
Triphasic combined oral contraceptives
All progesterone only pills except, Cerazette
All barrier methods, if intended to be used alone
Non-copper containing intra-uterine devices
Fertility awareness methods
Coitus interruptus

Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have either had a prior vasectomy agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to administration of the first dose of study treatment, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib
Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases

Stage IIIB, or distant metastases (including malignant pleural effusion) identified on PET-CT scan or biopsy (PET abnormalities that are negative for malignancy on biopsy will be considered on a case by case basis

Past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease
Patients who are known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)

Active second malignancy, i.e. patient known to have potentially fatal cancer present for which he/she may be (but not necessarily) currently receiving treatment; patients with a history of malignancy that has been completely treated, with no evidence of that cancer currently, are permitted to enroll in the trial provided all chemotherapy for prior malignancy was completed > 12 months prior and/or bone marrow transplant > 2 years prior

Patients who are currently receiving treatment with contraindicated corrected QT interval (QTc) prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers, if that treatment cannot be either discontinued or switched to a different medication prior to first day of study treatment.
Mean resting corrected QT interval (QTc) > 470 msec, obtained from 3 electrocardiograms (ECGs), using the screening clinic ECG machine derived QTc value
Any clinically important abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of resting ECG e.g. complete left bundle branch block, third degree heart block and second degree heart block

Any factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or risk of arrhythmic events such as heart failure, hypokalaemia, congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT syndrome or unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age in first degree relatives or any concomitant medication known to prolong the QT interval

Treatment with prohibited medications (concurrent anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal treatment [except corticosteroids and megesterolacetate], or immunotherapy) =< 14 days prior to treatment with osimertinib

Any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension and active bleeding diatheses, which in the investigator?s opinion makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the trial or which would jeopardize compliance with the protocol, or known active infection including chronic active hepatitis B, hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV); screening for chronic conditions is not required; patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) with negative HBV viral load on appropriate antiviral therapy will be permitted, if able to continue appropriate antiviral therapy throughout treatment period
Active tuberculosis
Signs or symptoms of infection within 2 weeks prior to first day of study
Therapeutic oral or intravenous (IV) antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to first day of study treatment:
Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system

Patients with known coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure not meeting the above criteria, or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50% must be on a stable medical regimen that is optimized in the opinion of the treating physician, in consultation with a cardiologist if appropriate, to be eligible

Patients who have experienced untreated and/or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions and/or have symptomatic cardiac dysfunction (unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous 3 months; coronary angioplasty, or stenting or bypass grafting within the past 6 months; cardiac ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication; any history of second (2nd) or third (3rd) degree atrioventricular conduction defects)
pregnant
breastfeeding

Presence of active gastrointestinal (GI) disease (including GI bleeding or ulceration) or other condition that could affect GI absorption (e.g. malabsorption syndrome, history of biliary tract disease), including refractory nausea or vomiting, or chronic GI disease which may affect absorption or tolerance to oral medications
History of hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of osimertinib or drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to osimertinib
Involvement in the planning and/or conduct of the study (applies to both investigator staff and/or staff at the study site)
Participation in another clinical study with an investigational product during the last 2 months or within five half-lives of the compound, whichever is longer

Uncontrolled medical, psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that interfere with the patient?s safety, ability to provide informed consent, or ability to comply with the protocol

criteria.text: Males and females >=18 years of age
Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), performed on a biopsy that occurred within the last 90 days.
Documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples by Clinical Laboratory Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-approved test
received no more than 28 days of treatment
no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment adverse events possibly related to treatment with the EGFR TKI
Positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer (mediastinal staging biopsy is allowed but not required)
Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (or CT if contraindication to MRI) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease
Documentation that the patient is a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon
The patient must have a tumor size >=1 centimeter (cm) in its longest diameter.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 0-1

Any unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinumtherapy-related neuropathy is allowed
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =< 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)

Bilirubin =< 1.5 x ULN, (Patients with documented Gilbert's syndrome and conjugated bilirubin within the normal range may be allowed into the study; in this event, it will be documented that the patient was eligible based on conjugated bilirubin levels)
Potassium and magnesium within normal range, patients may receive supplements to meet this requirement
Leukocytes > 3,000/microliter (mcL)
Hemoglobin >= 9 g/dL, with no blood transfusions in the 28 days prior to study entry
Absolute neutrophil count > 1,500/mcL
Platelets > 100,000/mcL
Creatinine Clearance (CrCl) > 50 mL/min for patients with serum creatinine (SCr) > 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)
Ability to swallow oral medications
must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment
agree to use highly effective contraception, during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib
Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP): women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation
Women NOT of childbearing potential: women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal

Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy and/or bilateral salpingectomy but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion; tubal occlusion is considered a highly effective method of birth control but does not absolutely exclude possibility of pregnancy; (the term occlusion refers to both occluding and ligating techniques that do not physically remove the oviducts)
Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP (e.g. undergo pregnancy testing etc., as required by the study protocol)
Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause; the following age-specific requirements apply:

Women under 50 years old will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments and with luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone levels in the postmenopausal range
Women over 50 years of age will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments
Acceptable contraception methods are:
Total sexual abstinence (abstinence must be for the total duration of the trial and the follow-up period)
Vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom (with participant assurance that partner received post-vasectomy confirmation of azoospermia)
Tubal occlusion plus male condom
Intra-uterine device - provided coils are copper-banded, plus male condom
Intra-uterine system (IUS) levonorgestrel IUS (e.g., Mirena), plus male condom
Medroxyprogesterone injections (Depo-Provera) plus male condom
Etonogestrel implants (e.g., Implanon, Norplan) plus male condom
Normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills, plus male condom
Norelgestromin / ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom
Intravaginal device (e.g., ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel) plus male condom
Cerazette (desogestrel) plus male condom (Cerazette is currently the only highly efficacious progesterone based pill)
Unacceptable Contraception Methods The following methods are considered not to be highly effective and are therefore not acceptable contraceptive methods:
Triphasic combined oral contraceptives
All progesterone only pills except, Cerazette
All barrier methods, if intended to be used alone
Non-copper containing intra-uterine devices
Fertility awareness methods

Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases

Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "Osimertinib in Treating Participants With Stage I-IIIA EGFR-mutant Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Before Surgery". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 55 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a biopsy to confirm non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the last 90 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my biopsy was about a month ago and it confirmed non-small cell lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had your tumor tested for an EGFR mutation (such as Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) using a CLIA-approved lab test? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, they told me the tumor has an EGFR mutation, specifically an exon 19 deletion.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if that EGFR mutation test was performed by a lab approved under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if the lab was CLIA-approved. I just know they told me about the mutation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you received any treatment for your lung cancer in the last 28 days? This includes chemotherapy, radiation, or other anti-cancer medications. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any chemotherapy, radiation, or immunotherapy in the last two months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had any side effects from your EGFR TKI treatment that were moderate or severe (grade 2 or higher)? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had any EGFR TKI treatment yet, so there are no side effects to report.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a PET-CT scan within the last 60 days to check the stage of your lung cancer? A PET-CT is a special imaging test that uses a small amount of radioactive material to show how organs and tissues are functioning.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't had a PET-CT scan recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a brain MRI (or CT if you can't have an MRI) within the last 60 days to check for spread of cancer? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't had a brain MRI or CT scan recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Has a surgeon certified by the American Board of Thoracic Surgery said you are a candidate for surgery to remove your lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know. I haven't spoken to a thoracic surgeon about being a candidate for surgery yet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you know the size of your tumor in its longest dimension? It needs to be at least 1 centimeter. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: On a scale of 0 to 1, how would you rate your ability to carry out normal daily activities? 0 means fully active, and 1 means restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out light work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently experiencing any side effects from previous cancer treatments that are more than mild (grade 1), such as significant pain, nausea, or fatigue? Hair loss or mild nerve tingling from platinum drugs are okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any cancer treatments yet, so I don't have any side effects from them.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you able to swallow pills or capsules easily?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can swallow oral medications without any trouble.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently pregnant or could you become pregnant during the study? If so, we would need a negative pregnancy test within 3 days before starting treatment.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am a man, so I am not pregnant.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you are sexually active with a partner who could become pregnant, are you willing to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days after your last dose of osimertinib?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I would agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days after the last dose.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever had a vasectomy?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I had a vasectomy ten years ago.

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any severe or uncontrolled medical conditions, such as high blood pressure, active bleeding issues, or an active infection like hepatitis or HIV?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any severe or uncontrolled medical conditions like high blood pressure, bleeding issues, or active infections.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with active tuberculosis?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with active tuberculosis.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any signs of infection like a fever, cough, or sore throat in the last two weeks.

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: agent

criteria.text: Males and females >=18 years of age
Histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), performed on a biopsy that occurred within the last 90 days.
Documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples by Clinical Laboratory Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)-approved test
received no more than 28 days of treatment
no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment adverse events possibly related to treatment with the EGFR TKI
Positron emission tomography (PET)-computed tomography (CT) within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer (mediastinal staging biopsy is allowed but not required)
Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) (or CT if contraindication to MRI) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease
Documentation that the patient is a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon
The patient must have a tumor size >=1 centimeter (cm) in its longest diameter.
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status (PS) of 0-1

Any unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinumtherapy-related neuropathy is allowed
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) =< 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)

Bilirubin =< 1.5 x ULN, (Patients with documented Gilbert's syndrome and conjugated bilirubin within the normal range may be allowed into the study; in this event, it will be documented that the patient was eligible based on conjugated bilirubin levels)
Potassium and magnesium within normal range, patients may receive supplements to meet this requirement
Leukocytes > 3,000/microliter (mcL)
Hemoglobin >= 9 g/dL, with no blood transfusions in the 28 days prior to study entry
Absolute neutrophil count > 1,500/mcL
Platelets > 100,000/mcL
Creatinine Clearance (CrCl) > 50 mL/min for patients with serum creatinine (SCr) > 1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN)
Ability to swallow oral medications
must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment
agree to use highly effective contraception, during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib
Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP): women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation
Women NOT of childbearing potential: women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal

Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy and/or bilateral salpingectomy but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion; tubal occlusion is considered a highly effective method of birth control but does not absolutely exclude possibility of pregnancy; (the term occlusion refers to both occluding and ligating techniques that do not physically remove the oviducts)
Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP (e.g. undergo pregnancy testing etc., as required by the study protocol)
Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause; the following age-specific requirements apply:

Women under 50 years old will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments and with luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone levels in the postmenopausal range
Women over 50 years of age will be considered postmenopausal if they have been amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments
Acceptable contraception methods are:
Total sexual abstinence (abstinence must be for the total duration of the trial and the follow-up period)
Vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom (with participant assurance that partner received post-vasectomy confirmation of azoospermia)
Tubal occlusion plus male condom
Intra-uterine device - provided coils are copper-banded, plus male condom
Intra-uterine system (IUS) levonorgestrel IUS (e.g., Mirena), plus male condom
Medroxyprogesterone injections (Depo-Provera) plus male condom
Etonogestrel implants (e.g., Implanon, Norplan) plus male condom
Normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills, plus male condom
Norelgestromin / ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom
Intravaginal device (e.g., ethinylestradiol and etonogestrel) plus male condom
Cerazette (desogestrel) plus male condom (Cerazette is currently the only highly efficacious progesterone based pill)
Unacceptable Contraception Methods The following methods are considered not to be highly effective and are therefore not acceptable contraceptive methods:
Triphasic combined oral contraceptives
All progesterone only pills except, Cerazette
All barrier methods, if intended to be used alone
Non-copper containing intra-uterine devices
Fertility awareness methods
Coitus interruptus

Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have either had a prior vasectomy agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to administration of the first dose of study treatment, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib
Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases

Stage IIIB, or distant metastases (including malignant pleural effusion) identified on PET-CT scan or biopsy (PET abnormalities that are negative for malignancy on biopsy will be considered on a case by case basis

Past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease
Patients who are known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)

Active second malignancy, i.e. patient known to have potentially fatal cancer present for which he/she may be (but not necessarily) currently receiving treatment; patients with a history of malignancy that has been completely treated, with no evidence of that cancer currently, are permitted to enroll in the trial provided all chemotherapy for prior malignancy was completed > 12 months prior and/or bone marrow transplant > 2 years prior

Patients who are currently receiving treatment with contraindicated corrected QT interval (QTc) prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers, if that treatment cannot be either discontinued or switched to a different medication prior to first day of study treatment.
Mean resting corrected QT interval (QTc) > 470 msec, obtained from 3 electrocardiograms (ECGs), using the screening clinic ECG machine derived QTc value
Any clinically important abnormalities in rhythm, conduction or morphology of resting ECG e.g. complete left bundle branch block, third degree heart block and second degree heart block

Any factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or risk of arrhythmic events such as heart failure, hypokalaemia, congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT syndrome or unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age in first degree relatives or any concomitant medication known to prolong the QT interval

Active tuberculosis
Signs or symptoms of infection within 2 weeks prior to first day of study
Therapeutic oral or intravenous (IV) antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to first day of study treatment:
Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system

Patients with known coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure not meeting the above criteria, or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50% must be on a stable medical regimen that is optimized in the opinion of the treating physician, in consultation with a cardiologist if appropriate, to be eligible

Patients who have experienced untreated and/or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions and/or have symptomatic cardiac dysfunction (unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous 3 months; coronary angioplasty, or stenting or bypass grafting within the past 6 months; cardiac ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication; any history of second (2nd) or third (3rd) degree atrioventricular conduction defects)
pregnant

History of hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of osimertinib or drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to osimertinib
Involvement in the planning and/or conduct of the study (applies to both investigator staff and/or staff at the study site)
Participation in another clinical study with an investigational product during the last 2 months or within five half-lives of the compound, whichever is longer

Uncontrolled medical, psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that interfere with the patient?s safety, ability to provide informed consent, or ability to comply with the protocol

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "A Trial of SHR-1316/Placebo in Combination With Chemotherapy in Patients With Resectable NSCLC". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. On a scale of 0 to 1, where 0 means fully active and 1 means restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory, how would you describe your current health status?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'd say I'm pretty active for my age, maybe a 0.2 or so. I still tend to wander around the farm, though I don't do the heavy lifting I used to.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been diagnosed with resectable Stage II, IIIA, or Selected IIIB non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has not yet been treated with cancer therapy?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Well, I did have that lung trouble a few years back the doctor called inflammation, and they gave me something through a drip, but I'm not sure if it was for cancer or what. I'm not a doctor, so I don't know the exact stage of anything.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. To be sure, have you ever been officially diagnosed with lung cancer (NSCLC) that was confirmed by a biopsy and found to be operable (resectable)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I had a biopsy or if it was officially called cancer. I just know I had some lung trouble and got a drip treatment a while back. I don't have the medical records to confirm the exact diagnosis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever had a thoracic surgeon evaluate you to confirm that your lung condition could be completely removed with surgery for a cure?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't think so. I just saw a general doctor for my lungs back then, not a surgeon. I'm not sure if anyone ever talked to me about removing it with surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent scans (like a CT or PET scan) that showed a tumor or spot in your body that doctors could measure to track its size?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about any recent scans. I haven't had any tests done since that lung trouble a few years ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent blood tests (like within the last 2 weeks) to check your liver, kidney, and blood cell levels?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't had any blood work done recently, not even in the last two weeks. I haven't had any tests since that lung trouble a few years back.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently using any form of birth control, or are you abstinent from sexual activity?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm a 70-year-old man, so I don't use birth control. I'm married, but we've been past that stage of life for a long time now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received any systemic anti-cancer treatments (like chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) specifically for lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I think they gave me something through a drip a while back, but I am not sure what it was for. I'm not a doctor, so I can't say for sure if it was specifically for lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. To be sure, did the treatment you received through the drip specifically target your lung cancer, or was it for a different condition?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I really can't say for sure. I just know I had some lung trouble and got a drip treatment a while back, but I don't have the medical records to confirm exactly what it was for.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any known or suspected autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or Crohn's disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about any of those autoimmune diseases. I've never been diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or Crohn's disease, but I'm not sure if I have any others.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand better, have you ever been told by a doctor that you have an autoimmune condition, or do you currently take any medication specifically for an autoimmune disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never been told I have an autoimmune condition, and I don't take any meds for that sort of thing. I just take the usual vitamins and such for my age.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with any other type of cancer (besides lung cancer) in the last 5 years?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any other cancers besides that lung trouble. I've been pretty lucky in that regard.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a history of pneumonitis, interstitial lung disease, or any other severe lung conditions that affect how your lungs work?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Well, I did have some lung trouble a few years ago, and the doctor called it inflammation. I'm not sure if that counts as pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease, but it did affect my breathing a bit back then.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, was that lung inflammation ever diagnosed as pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know if you have any other severe lung conditions that affect your breathing.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if the doctor used those specific terms back then, but it was definitely inflammation that made it hard to breathe. I don't have the records to confirm the exact diagnosis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with significant heart or blood vessel disease, such as a heart attack, stroke, or heart failure?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any heart attacks or strokes. My heart seems to be doing fine, thank goodness.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a significant bleeding disorder or condition that causes excessive bleeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never had any trouble with bleeding. I'm not sure if that's a medical term, but I don't have any conditions that make me bleed too much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, have you ever been diagnosed with a bleeding disorder, such as hemophilia, von Willebrand disease, or low platelets?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never been diagnosed with any of those bleeding disorders like hemophilia or low platelets. I've always been able to stop a cut pretty quickly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with an arteriovenous thrombotic event? This refers to a blood clot that forms in an abnormal connection between an artery and a vein. If you're not sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know what an arteriovenous thrombotic event is, but I've never had any blood clots or issues with my veins and arteries that I know of.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with HIV. I've never had any issues with that, thank goodness.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C? These are viral infections that affect the liver. If you're not sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had hepatitis B or hepatitis C. I've been pretty healthy in that regard.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to monoclonal antibodies or other protein drugs? These are medicines made from proteins, often used for cancer or autoimmune conditions. If you're not sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had an allergic reaction to any medicine, including those protein drugs you mentioned. I've always been fine with my medications.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently allergic to SHR-1316 or any of the chemotherapy medicines used in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never had an allergic reaction to any medicine, so I don't think I'm allergic to those study drugs. I've always been fine with my medications.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, have you ever had an allergic reaction specifically to SHR-1316 or any of the chemotherapy drugs used in this study? If you're not sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never had an allergic reaction to any medicine, so I don't think I'm allergic to those study drugs. I've always been fine with my medications.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or planning to become pregnant during the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Me? No, I am not pregnant. I'm a 70-year-old man, so that's not something I have to worry about!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have a diagnosed psychiatric condition, such as depression, anxiety, or bipolar disorder, that requires ongoing treatment or management?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with any of those. I've always been in good spirits, though I do like to take my time wandering around the farm.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a substance abuse disorder, such as alcohol or drug dependence?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I used to drink too much, years back. Not so much now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, have you ever been diagnosed with alcohol or drug dependence, or received treatment for it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I was ever officially diagnosed with dependence or if I went to any treatment programs. I just know I used to drink too much years ago, but not so much now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with or suspected to have had a COVID-19 infection?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I do not think I have had COVID, but who knows. There was a bug going round at church a while back, it could have been that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, have you ever had a positive test for COVID-19, or were you ever told by a doctor that you likely had it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't think I ever had a positive test for it, and no doctor ever told me I likely had it. I just know there was a bug going around at church, but I never got tested.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. In the last 14 days, have you had close contact with anyone who has known or suspected COVID-19?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Hard to say. There was a bug going round at church, it could have been COVID. I don't keep track of who was sick exactly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us decide, have you spent time (like sitting close or sharing a room) with anyone in the last 14 days who was confirmed to have COVID-19 or was told by a doctor they likely had it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know for sure. I wasn't keeping track of who was sick at church, so I can't say if I sat close to anyone with a confirmed case.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

criteria.text: Patients must be capable of giving signed informed consent, which includes a mandatory genetic informed consent and compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent forms (ICFs) and in this protocol.
Provision of signed and dated, written ICFs must occur prior to any mandatory study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses.
ICF1 must be signed and dated prior to any study procedures and prior to the planned surgical resection of the primary NSCLC, with the exceptions noted below.
In these cases, a whole blood sample and resected tumor tissue must be collected and sent to the diagnostic lab as soon as possible after ICF1 is signed for development of the personalized panel.
A plasma sample must still be collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery, even if creation of the personalized panel for MRD detection is delayed.
Age ≥18 years at the time of screening.
Individuals who have diagnosis of histologically confirmed NSCLC (WHO 2015 classification) with resectable (stage II-III) disease (according to IASLC Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology v8.0).
Select (ie, T3N2 or T4N2) stage IIIB patients will be eligible, provided that they are upstaged to T3N2 or T4N2 based on confirmed pathology.
Patients who are staged asT3N2 or T4N2 prior to surgery are not eligible.
A contrast-enhanced CT or MRI scan of the chest must have been done for surgical planning prior to surgery.
In the absence of pre-operative FDG-PET CT imaging, pre-operative contrast-enhanced CT imaging or MRI scan must cover liver and adrenal glands.
Brain MRI (preferred) or brain CT with IV contrast is required for complete staging of the tumor.
Complete resection of the primary NSCLC is mandatory.

The primary tumor must be deemed resectable by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon certified or trained according to local standards and who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients undergoing wedge resection are not eligible for this study.
Note: Patients undergoing segmentectomy must have tumors less than 2 cm in maximum diameter.
The surgeon performing the resection should remove all gross disease by the end of surgery.
All surgical margins of resection must be macroscopically negative for tumor.

Pathology and/or operative reports must include the examination of at least 2 different mediastinal lymph node (N2) levels, one of which is the subcarinal node-group (level 7) and the second of which is lobe-specific (defined below).
However, the surgeon must clearly document in the operative report or in a separate written statement that the lymph node level was explored and no lymph nodes were present.
Normal appearing lymph nodes, if present, must be biopsied or removed.
Exploration of nodes must clearly be documented in medical file if not recorded in operative report.

Note: Lobe-specific lymph node stations are classified based on the location of the primary tumor as follows (based on IASLC 2009 lymph node map terminology [Rusch et al 2009]): Stations 2R and 4R for right upper lobe or middle lobe tumors, stations 4L, 5, and 6 for left upper lobe tumors, stations 8 and 9 for lower lobe tumors of both sides (Adachi et al 2017, Rami-Porta et al 2005).
No extracapsular nodal extension of the tumor is observed in resected mediastinal N2 lymph nodes.
All patients who enrol in the study prior to surgery must have a pre-surgical plasma sample collected for MRD evaluation.
Confirmation of suitable samples of resected tumor tissue and whole blood for WES of tumor and germline DNA, respectively, and creation of Sponsor-approved personalized panel for MRD detection.
Tumor tissue and whole blood samples must be provided to the diagnostic laboratory for development of the personalized panel as soon as possible.
Germline sequencing of whole blood is mandatory.
Established MRD status (MRD+ or MRD-) based on Sponsor-approved personalized assay of a plasma sample collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery.
Known tumor PD-L1 status determined at a central reference laboratory testing service using a validated Ventana SP263 PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay prior randomization.
Post-operative CT scan of the chest (including liver and adrenal glands) performed within 28 days + 7 days prior to randomization.
ICF2 must be signed and dated after MRD status is determined and prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses outlined in SoAs in Table 2 and Table 3.
Randomization must occur within the 12 weeks (+ 7 days) following surgery.
WHO/Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

Complete postoperative wound healing must have occurred prior to randomization; patients must have recovered from all acute, reversible toxic effects from prior treatments (excluding alopecia) that could potentially adversely impact further administration of durvalumab/placebo or chemotherapy according to the Investigator's judgment.
Eligible to tolerate 4 cycles of platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy
Adequate organ and marrow function as described in the protocol
Must have a life expectancy of at least
Post-operative imaging demonstrating unequivocal evidence of disease recurrence or tissue biopsy-proven disease recurrence.
In the event of lymphadenopathy on imaging that would lead to exclusion, histopathological confirmation of lymph node metastasis should be obtained prior to excluding a patient from the study.
EGFR-mutant and/or ALK-translocation-positive, as assessed either from a pre-surgical biopsy sample (preferred) or the resected tumor tissue (if biopsy was not evaluable or available).
Where EGFR/ALK results are obtained from a pre-surgical tissue biopsy as part of standard local practice, the patient must be confirmed EGFR/ALK wild-type prior to enrolling in the study.
Results obtained from testing the patient's primary tumor tissue during screening for another AstraZeneca study may be used in this study.
Results from local testing of a pre-surgical biopsy.
All local EGFR/ALK testing performed locally must be performed using a well-validated, local regulatory-approved test.
Mixed small cell and NSCLC histology.

Require re-resection or are deemed to have unresectable NSCLC by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients who are candidates to undergo only wedge resections.
History of allogeneic organ or bone marrow transplantation.
Non-leukocyte-depleted whole blood transfusion within 120 days of genetic sample collection.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease [eg, colitis or Crohn's disease], diverticulitis [with the exception of diverticulosis], systemic lupus erythematosus, Sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome [granulomatosis with polyangiitis, Graves' disease, rheumatoid arthritis, hypophysitis, uveitis, etc]).

Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, active ILD, serious chronic gastrointestinal conditions associated with diarrhea, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, substantially increase risk of incurring AEs, or compromise the ability of the patient to give written informed consent.
History of another primary malignancy, except for
History of active primary immunodeficiency

Active infection, including tuberculosis (clinical evaluation that includes clinical history, physical examination, and radiographic findings, and tuberculosis testing in line with local practice), hepatitis B (HBV; known positive HBV surface antigen [HBsAg] result), hepatitis C (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus infection (positive HIV 1/2 antibodies).
Patients positive for HCV antibody are eligible only if polymerase chain reaction is negative for HCV RNA.
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the IPs or any of the IP excipients.
Any medical contraindication to treatment with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as listed in the local labeling.
Received any prior adjuvant therapy for NSCLC or any prior exposure to durvalumab.
Any concurrent chemotherapy, IP, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.
Radiotherapy treatment for NSCLC in the neoadjuvant setting.
Radiotherapy treatment to more than 30% of the bone marrow or with a wide field of radiation within 4 weeks of the first dose of IP.
Receipt of live attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Major surgical procedure (as defined by the Investigator) within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Participation in another clinical study with an IP administered since completion of surgery.
Previous IP assignment in the present study.
Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (noninterventional) clinical study, or during the follow-up period of an interventional study.
Prior randomization or treatment in a previous durvalumab clinical study regardless of treatment group assignment.
Patients who are never-smokers; defined as no more than 100 cigarettes or its equivalent in his/her lifetime.
pregnant
breastfeeding
male or female patients of reproductive potential who are not willing to employ effective birth control from screening to 90 days after the last dose of durvalumab/placebo
Judgment by the Investigator that the patient should not participate in the study if the patient is unlikely to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements.
