criteria.text: Patients must be capable of giving signed informed consent, which includes a mandatory genetic informed consent and compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent forms (ICFs) and in this protocol.
Provision of signed and dated, written ICFs must occur prior to any mandatory study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses.
ICF1 must be signed and dated prior to any study procedures and prior to the planned surgical resection of the primary NSCLC, with the exceptions noted below.
In these cases, a whole blood sample and resected tumor tissue must be collected and sent to the diagnostic lab as soon as possible after ICF1 is signed for development of the personalized panel.
A plasma sample must still be collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery, even if creation of the personalized panel for MRD detection is delayed.
Age ≥18 years at the time of screening.
Individuals who have diagnosis of histologically confirmed NSCLC (WHO 2015 classification) with resectable (stage II-III) disease (according to IASLC Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology v8.0).
Select (ie, T3N2 or T4N2) stage IIIB patients will be eligible, provided that they are upstaged to T3N2 or T4N2 based on confirmed pathology.
Patients who are staged asT3N2 or T4N2 prior to surgery are not eligible.
A contrast-enhanced CT or MRI scan of the chest must have been done for surgical planning prior to surgery.
In the absence of pre-operative FDG-PET CT imaging, pre-operative contrast-enhanced CT imaging or MRI scan must cover liver and adrenal glands.
Brain MRI (preferred) or brain CT with IV contrast is required for complete staging of the tumor.
Complete resection of the primary NSCLC is mandatory.

The primary tumor must be deemed resectable by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon certified or trained according to local standards and who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients undergoing wedge resection are not eligible for this study.
Note: Patients undergoing segmentectomy must have tumors less than 2 cm in maximum diameter.
The surgeon performing the resection should remove all gross disease by the end of surgery.
All surgical margins of resection must be macroscopically negative for tumor.

Pathology and/or operative reports must include the examination of at least 2 different mediastinal lymph node (N2) levels, one of which is the subcarinal node-group (level 7) and the second of which is lobe-specific (defined below).
However, the surgeon must clearly document in the operative report or in a separate written statement that the lymph node level was explored and no lymph nodes were present.
Normal appearing lymph nodes, if present, must be biopsied or removed.
Exploration of nodes must clearly be documented in medical file if not recorded in operative report.

Note: Lobe-specific lymph node stations are classified based on the location of the primary tumor as follows (based on IASLC 2009 lymph node map terminology [Rusch et al 2009]): Stations 2R and 4R for right upper lobe or middle lobe tumors, stations 4L, 5, and 6 for left upper lobe tumors, stations 8 and 9 for lower lobe tumors of both sides (Adachi et al 2017, Rami-Porta et al 2005).
No extracapsular nodal extension of the tumor is observed in resected mediastinal N2 lymph nodes.
All patients who enrol in the study prior to surgery must have a pre-surgical plasma sample collected for MRD evaluation.
Confirmation of suitable samples of resected tumor tissue and whole blood for WES of tumor and germline DNA, respectively, and creation of Sponsor-approved personalized panel for MRD detection.
Tumor tissue and whole blood samples must be provided to the diagnostic laboratory for development of the personalized panel as soon as possible.
Germline sequencing of whole blood is mandatory.
Established MRD status (MRD+ or MRD-) based on Sponsor-approved personalized assay of a plasma sample collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery.
Known tumor PD-L1 status determined at a central reference laboratory testing service using a validated Ventana SP263 PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay prior randomization.
Post-operative CT scan of the chest (including liver and adrenal glands) performed within 28 days + 7 days prior to randomization.
ICF2 must be signed and dated after MRD status is determined and prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses outlined in SoAs in Table 2 and Table 3.
Randomization must occur within the 12 weeks (+ 7 days) following surgery.
WHO/Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

Complete postoperative wound healing must have occurred prior to randomization; patients must have recovered from all acute, reversible toxic effects from prior treatments (excluding alopecia) that could potentially adversely impact further administration of durvalumab/placebo or chemotherapy according to the Investigator's judgment.
Eligible to tolerate 4 cycles of platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy
Adequate organ and marrow function as described in the protocol
Must have a life expectancy of at least
Post-operative imaging demonstrating unequivocal evidence of disease recurrence or tissue biopsy-proven disease recurrence.
In the event of lymphadenopathy on imaging that would lead to exclusion, histopathological confirmation of lymph node metastasis should be obtained prior to excluding a patient from the study.
EGFR-mutant and/or ALK-translocation-positive, as assessed either from a pre-surgical biopsy sample (preferred) or the resected tumor tissue (if biopsy was not evaluable or available).
Where EGFR/ALK results are obtained from a pre-surgical tissue biopsy as part of standard local practice, the patient must be confirmed EGFR/ALK wild-type prior to enrolling in the study.
Results obtained from testing the patient's primary tumor tissue during screening for another AstraZeneca study may be used in this study.
Results from local testing of a pre-surgical biopsy.
All local EGFR/ALK testing performed locally must be performed using a well-validated, local regulatory-approved test.
Mixed small cell and NSCLC histology.

Require re-resection or are deemed to have unresectable NSCLC by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients who are candidates to undergo only wedge resections.
History of allogeneic organ or bone marrow transplantation.
Non-leukocyte-depleted whole blood transfusion within 120 days of genetic sample collection.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease [eg, colitis or Crohn's disease], diverticulitis [with the exception of diverticulosis], systemic lupus erythematosus, Sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome [granulomatosis with polyangiitis, Graves' disease, rheumatoid arthritis, hypophysitis, uveitis, etc]).

Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, active ILD, serious chronic gastrointestinal conditions associated with diarrhea, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, substantially increase risk of incurring AEs, or compromise the ability of the patient to give written informed consent.
History of another primary malignancy, except for
History of active primary immunodeficiency

Active infection, including tuberculosis (clinical evaluation that includes clinical history, physical examination, and radiographic findings, and tuberculosis testing in line with local practice), hepatitis B (HBV; known positive HBV surface antigen [HBsAg] result), hepatitis C (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus infection (positive HIV 1/2 antibodies).
Patients positive for HCV antibody are eligible only if polymerase chain reaction is negative for HCV RNA.
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the IPs or any of the IP excipients.
Any medical contraindication to treatment with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as listed in the local labeling.
Received any prior adjuvant therapy for NSCLC or any prior exposure to durvalumab.
Any concurrent chemotherapy, IP, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.
Radiotherapy treatment for NSCLC in the neoadjuvant setting.
Radiotherapy treatment to more than 30% of the bone marrow or with a wide field of radiation within 4 weeks of the first dose of IP.
Receipt of live attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Major surgical procedure (as defined by the Investigator) within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Participation in another clinical study with an IP administered since completion of surgery.
Previous IP assignment in the present study.
Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (noninterventional) clinical study, or during the follow-up period of an interventional study.
Prior randomization or treatment in a previous durvalumab clinical study regardless of treatment group assignment.
Patients who are never-smokers; defined as no more than 100 cigarettes or its equivalent in his/her lifetime.
pregnant
breastfeeding
male or female patients of reproductive potential who are not willing to employ effective birth control from screening to 90 days after the last dose of durvalumab/placebo
Judgment by the Investigator that the patient should not participate in the study if the patient is unlikely to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements.

criteria.text: Patients must be capable of giving signed informed consent, which includes a mandatory genetic informed consent and compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent forms (ICFs) and in this protocol.
Provision of signed and dated, written ICFs must occur prior to any mandatory study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses.
ICF1 must be signed and dated prior to any study procedures and prior to the planned surgical resection of the primary NSCLC, with the exceptions noted below.
In these cases, a whole blood sample and resected tumor tissue must be collected and sent to the diagnostic lab as soon as possible after ICF1 is signed for development of the personalized panel.
A plasma sample must still be collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery, even if creation of the personalized panel for MRD detection is delayed.
Age ≥18 years at the time of screening.
Individuals who have diagnosis of histologically confirmed NSCLC (WHO 2015 classification) with resectable (stage II-III) disease (according to IASLC Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology v8.0).
Select (ie, T3N2 or T4N2) stage IIIB patients will be eligible, provided that they are upstaged to T3N2 or T4N2 based on confirmed pathology.
Patients who are staged asT3N2 or T4N2 prior to surgery are not eligible.
A contrast-enhanced CT or MRI scan of the chest must have been done for surgical planning prior to surgery.
In the absence of pre-operative FDG-PET CT imaging, pre-operative contrast-enhanced CT imaging or MRI scan must cover liver and adrenal glands.
Brain MRI (preferred) or brain CT with IV contrast is required for complete staging of the tumor.
Complete resection of the primary NSCLC is mandatory.

The primary tumor must be deemed resectable by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon certified or trained according to local standards and who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients undergoing wedge resection are not eligible for this study.
Note: Patients undergoing segmentectomy must have tumors less than 2 cm in maximum diameter.
The surgeon performing the resection should remove all gross disease by the end of surgery.
All surgical margins of resection must be macroscopically negative for tumor.

Pathology and/or operative reports must include the examination of at least 2 different mediastinal lymph node (N2) levels, one of which is the subcarinal node-group (level 7) and the second of which is lobe-specific (defined below).
However, the surgeon must clearly document in the operative report or in a separate written statement that the lymph node level was explored and no lymph nodes were present.
Normal appearing lymph nodes, if present, must be biopsied or removed.
Exploration of nodes must clearly be documented in medical file if not recorded in operative report.

Note: Lobe-specific lymph node stations are classified based on the location of the primary tumor as follows (based on IASLC 2009 lymph node map terminology [Rusch et al 2009]): Stations 2R and 4R for right upper lobe or middle lobe tumors, stations 4L, 5, and 6 for left upper lobe tumors, stations 8 and 9 for lower lobe tumors of both sides (Adachi et al 2017, Rami-Porta et al 2005).
No extracapsular nodal extension of the tumor is observed in resected mediastinal N2 lymph nodes.
All patients who enrol in the study prior to surgery must have a pre-surgical plasma sample collected for MRD evaluation.
Confirmation of suitable samples of resected tumor tissue and whole blood for WES of tumor and germline DNA, respectively, and creation of Sponsor-approved personalized panel for MRD detection.
Tumor tissue and whole blood samples must be provided to the diagnostic laboratory for development of the personalized panel as soon as possible.
Germline sequencing of whole blood is mandatory.
Established MRD status (MRD+ or MRD-) based on Sponsor-approved personalized assay of a plasma sample collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery.
Known tumor PD-L1 status determined at a central reference laboratory testing service using a validated Ventana SP263 PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay prior randomization.
Post-operative CT scan of the chest (including liver and adrenal glands) performed within 28 days + 7 days prior to randomization.
ICF2 must be signed and dated after MRD status is determined and prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses outlined in SoAs in Table 2 and Table 3.
Randomization must occur within the 12 weeks (+ 7 days) following surgery.
WHO/Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

Complete postoperative wound healing must have occurred prior to randomization; patients must have recovered from all acute, reversible toxic effects from prior treatments (excluding alopecia) that could potentially adversely impact further administration of durvalumab/placebo or chemotherapy according to the Investigator's judgment.
Eligible to tolerate 4 cycles of platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy
Adequate organ and marrow function as described in the protocol
Must have a life expectancy of at least
Post-operative imaging demonstrating unequivocal evidence of disease recurrence or tissue biopsy-proven disease recurrence.
In the event of lymphadenopathy on imaging that would lead to exclusion, histopathological confirmation of lymph node metastasis should be obtained prior to excluding a patient from the study.
EGFR-mutant and/or ALK-translocation-positive, as assessed either from a pre-surgical biopsy sample (preferred) or the resected tumor tissue (if biopsy was not evaluable or available).
Where EGFR/ALK results are obtained from a pre-surgical tissue biopsy as part of standard local practice, the patient must be confirmed EGFR/ALK wild-type prior to enrolling in the study.
Results obtained from testing the patient's primary tumor tissue during screening for another AstraZeneca study may be used in this study.
Results from local testing of a pre-surgical biopsy.
All local EGFR/ALK testing performed locally must be performed using a well-validated, local regulatory-approved test.
Mixed small cell and NSCLC histology.

Require re-resection or are deemed to have unresectable NSCLC by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients who are candidates to undergo only wedge resections.
History of allogeneic organ or bone marrow transplantation.
Non-leukocyte-depleted whole blood transfusion within 120 days of genetic sample collection.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease [eg, colitis or Crohn's disease], diverticulitis [with the exception of diverticulosis], systemic lupus erythematosus, Sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome [granulomatosis with polyangiitis, Graves' disease, rheumatoid arthritis, hypophysitis, uveitis, etc]).

Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, active ILD, serious chronic gastrointestinal conditions associated with diarrhea, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, substantially increase risk of incurring AEs, or compromise the ability of the patient to give written informed consent.
History of another primary malignancy, except for
History of active primary immunodeficiency

Active infection, including tuberculosis (clinical evaluation that includes clinical history, physical examination, and radiographic findings, and tuberculosis testing in line with local practice), hepatitis B (HBV; known positive HBV surface antigen [HBsAg] result), hepatitis C (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus infection (positive HIV 1/2 antibodies).
Patients positive for HCV antibody are eligible only if polymerase chain reaction is negative for HCV RNA.
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the IPs or any of the IP excipients.
Any medical contraindication to treatment with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as listed in the local labeling.
Received any prior adjuvant therapy for NSCLC or any prior exposure to durvalumab.
Any concurrent chemotherapy, IP, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.
Radiotherapy treatment for NSCLC in the neoadjuvant setting.
Radiotherapy treatment to more than 30% of the bone marrow or with a wide field of radiation within 4 weeks of the first dose of IP.
Receipt of live attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Major surgical procedure (as defined by the Investigator) within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Participation in another clinical study with an IP administered since completion of surgery.
Previous IP assignment in the present study.
Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (noninterventional) clinical study, or during the follow-up period of an interventional study.
Prior randomization or treatment in a previous durvalumab clinical study regardless of treatment group assignment.
Patients who are never-smokers; defined as no more than 100 cigarettes or its equivalent in his/her lifetime.
pregnant
breastfeeding
male or female patients of reproductive potential who are not willing to employ effective birth control from screening to 90 days after the last dose of durvalumab/placebo
Judgment by the Investigator that the patient should not participate in the study if the patient is unlikely to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements.

criteria.text: Sign the informed consent
Pathologically or cytologically diagnosed with metastatic/relapsed advanced NSCLC
with measurable lesions (according to RECIST 1.1)
Previously received at least two systemic therapies, allowing for third-line or higher chemotherapy or unable to tolerate chemotherapy

Patients with negative results for driver gene testing or patients with positive results who have already received relevant targeted drugs or systemic anti-tumor treatments and are either resistant or unable to tolerate them
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0-2.
Expected survival time ≥ 3 months
renal function with creatinine clearance rate ≥ 60 mL/min
liver function with bilirubin ≤ 1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN)
ALT/AST ≤ 2.5× ULN
absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5×10\^9/L
platelet count ≥ 100×10\^9/L
hemoglobin ≥ 90g/L

Good coagulation function, defined as an international normalized ratio (INR) or prothrombin time (PT) ≤ 1.5× ULN; if the subject is on anticoagulation therapy, PT should be within the intended therapeutic range of the anticoagulant

Female patients of childbearing potential must agree to use contraception (e.g., intrauterine device, contraceptives, or condoms) during the study and for 6 months after the study ends; must not be breastfeeding and must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment.
Male patients must agree to use contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study ends
Patients with well-controlled pleural or peritoneal effusions that do not cause grade 2 or higher respiratory syndrome (≥ CTCAE grade 2) can be included

Patients without clinical symptoms of intracranial hypertension caused by brain metastases or with brain metastasis symptoms that are stable after prior treatment (radiation therapy or surgery) of brain or meningeal metastasis (usually requiring more than 4 weeks post-radiation therapy)
Previously failed treatment with multi-target anti-angiogenic drugs, such as anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, lenvatinib, etc.
The use of bevacizumab is allowed, but the last administration must be more than 3 weeks before enrollment
Small cell lung cancer (including small cell carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer mixed with other types of tumors)
Testing positive for driver genes but not treated with TKIs
Tumor invasion of large blood vessels
central squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with cavitation
non-small cell lung cancer with hemoptysis (>5ml/day)
where the tumor is likely to invade important blood vessels and cause fatal bleeding during the subsequent study period
Accompanied by other types of malignant tumors within the past 5 years or currently
Planning to receive systemic anti-tumor therapy within 4 weeks before enrollment or during the study period
received extended-field radiation therapy (EF-RT) within 4 weeks before enrollment or limited-field radiation therapy within 2 weeks before enrollment
Unremitting toxic reactions caused by previous treatment, CTCAE grade >1, excluding hair loss
Various factors affecting oral medication (such as inability to swallow, gastrointestinal resection, chronic diarrhea, bowel obstruction)
Pleural effusion or ascites leading to respiratory syndrome (≥CTCAE grade 2)
Symptoms of brain metastasis not controlled and treated within 2 months
Presence of any severe or uncontrolled disease
Major surgery, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days before enrollment
Bleeding diathesis or history of significant bleeding, regardless of severity; any wound, ulcer, or fracture that has not healed following a bleeding or bleeding event (≥CTCAE grade 3)
Arterial/venous thrombosis within 6 months, such as cerebrovascular accident (including transient ischemic attack), venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism
History of substance abuse that cannot be quit
diagnosed with psychiatric disorders
Participated in other clinical trials of anti-tumor drugs within 4 weeks
Diagnosed with diseases that severely jeopardize patient safety or affect the completion of this study
Known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (i.e., HIV 1/2 antibody positive)
untreated active hepatitis B
active HCV infection

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "Efficacy and Safety of Vorolanib Monotherapy As Third-line or Later Treatment for Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Patients: a Single-arm, Prospective, Open-label Phase II Clinical Study". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to sign the informed consent form for this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am happy to sign the informed consent. To lay out my history up front, I had an open biopsy three weeks ago, have no history of substance abuse, and have not taken part in any other clinical trials.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body or come back after treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I was pathologically diagnosed with non-small cell lung cancer. It relapsed last year and is currently advanced and metastatic.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any imaging scans (like a CT or MRI) in the last 4 weeks that showed tumors or lesions that can be measured?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the specific results of my recent imaging scans. I don't have that information on hand right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received at least two different systemic cancer treatments (such as chemotherapy or targeted therapy) before this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I have had three systemic therapies before now: chemotherapy twice and immunotherapy once.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had genetic testing for driver genes (like EGFR or ALK)? If positive, have you already tried the specific targeted drugs for those genes?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have had genetic testing for driver genes like EGFR or ALK, or if I have tried targeted drugs for them.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. On a scale of 0 to 2, how would you rate your ability to carry out daily activities? A score of 0 means fully active, 1 means restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory, and 2 means capable of self-care but unable to work.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I would rate my ability to carry out daily activities as a 1. I am restricted in physically strenuous activity but I am still ambulatory.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for at least 3 more months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know my exact prognosis or life expectancy, so I'm not sure if I can guarantee I'll live for at least 3 more months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently breastfeeding? Also, are you able to use effective contraception (like a pill, IUD, or condoms) during the study and for 6 months after it ends?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I am not breastfeeding and I would agree to use contraception for six months after the study. I have not had a pregnancy test yet.

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a serum or urine pregnancy test within the last 7 days, and was the result negative?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have not had a pregnancy test yet.

transcript.text: Thanks. Since you haven't had a pregnancy test yet, would you be willing to have one done within the next 7 days to confirm a negative result?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, do you agree to use effective contraception (like condoms or a partner using a barrier method) during the study and for 6 months after it ends?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I agree to use effective contraception during the study and for 6 months after it ends.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have fluid buildup in your chest (pleural effusion) or abdomen (peritoneal effusion) that is causing moderate or severe breathing problems?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have fluid buildup in my chest or abdomen causing breathing problems. I haven't mentioned those specific symptoms.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have symptoms of increased pressure in the brain (like severe headaches or vision changes) caused by brain metastases, or have you had radiation or surgery for brain metastases in the last 4 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have information regarding brain metastases or recent brain radiation/surgery in my facts, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you previously received treatment with multi-target anti-angiogenic drugs, such as anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, or lenvatinib?

transcript.text: Have you ever received a treatment called bevacizumab? If yes, when was your last dose?

transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, have you ever been diagnosed with small cell lung cancer, or a type of lung cancer that mixes small cell and non-small cell features?

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by your doctor that your tumor has grown into or invaded any large blood vessels?

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told that your lung tumor is a type called 'squamous cell carcinoma' and that it has a hollow space or cavity inside it?

transcript.text: Thanks. In the last 4 weeks, have you coughed up any blood? If so, was it more than 5 milliliters (about one teaspoon) per day?

transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your recent scans, does your doctor think there is a risk that the tumor could invade important blood vessels and cause serious bleeding?

transcript.text: Thanks. To make sure you can take the study medication by mouth, do you have any trouble swallowing, or have you had stomach or bowel surgery, chronic diarrhea, or a bowel obstruction?

transcript.text: I don't have information regarding swallowing difficulties, stomach or bowel surgery, chronic diarrhea, or bowel obstruction, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any symptoms related to brain metastasis that were not controlled or treated within the last 2 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have information regarding symptoms related to brain metastasis in the last 2 months, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently experiencing any severe symptoms or signs that your cancer is not well-controlled?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have specific information on whether my cancer is currently well-controlled or if I have severe uncontrolled symptoms right now, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a bleeding problem, or any wound, ulcer, or fracture that hasn't healed after a significant bleeding event?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have information regarding any history of bleeding problems or unhealed wounds/fractures, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any blood clots, such as a stroke, TIA, or pulmonary embolism, in the last 6 months? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have information regarding any history of blood clots, strokes, or pulmonary embolisms, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder, such as depression or anxiety? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have been treated for depression in the past.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any other serious health conditions that might make it unsafe for you to participate in this study or complete it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have information about any other serious health conditions beyond what I've already mentioned, so I'm not sure if there are any that would make participation unsafe.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) or tested positive for it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have any information regarding an HIV diagnosis or test results, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with hepatitis B, or are you currently being treated for it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have never had hepatitis B.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with hepatitis C (HCV) or told you have an active hepatitis C infection?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have any information regarding a diagnosis of hepatitis C or an active infection, so I'm not sure about that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

criteria.text: Sign the informed consent
Pathologically or cytologically diagnosed with metastatic/relapsed advanced NSCLC
with measurable lesions (according to RECIST 1.1)
Previously received at least two systemic therapies, allowing for third-line or higher chemotherapy or unable to tolerate chemotherapy

Patients with negative results for driver gene testing or patients with positive results who have already received relevant targeted drugs or systemic anti-tumor treatments and are either resistant or unable to tolerate them
Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0-2.
Expected survival time ≥ 3 months
renal function with creatinine clearance rate ≥ 60 mL/min
liver function with bilirubin ≤ 1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN)
ALT/AST ≤ 2.5× ULN
absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5×10\^9/L
platelet count ≥ 100×10\^9/L
hemoglobin ≥ 90g/L

Good coagulation function, defined as an international normalized ratio (INR) or prothrombin time (PT) ≤ 1.5× ULN; if the subject is on anticoagulation therapy, PT should be within the intended therapeutic range of the anticoagulant

Female patients of childbearing potential must agree to use contraception (e.g., intrauterine device, contraceptives, or condoms) during the study and for 6 months after the study ends; must not be breastfeeding and must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment.
Male patients must agree to use contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study ends
Patients with well-controlled pleural or peritoneal effusions that do not cause grade 2 or higher respiratory syndrome (≥ CTCAE grade 2) can be included

Patients without clinical symptoms of intracranial hypertension caused by brain metastases or with brain metastasis symptoms that are stable after prior treatment (radiation therapy or surgery) of brain or meningeal metastasis (usually requiring more than 4 weeks post-radiation therapy)
Previously failed treatment with multi-target anti-angiogenic drugs, such as anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, lenvatinib, etc.
The use of bevacizumab is allowed, but the last administration must be more than 3 weeks before enrollment
Small cell lung cancer (including small cell carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer mixed with other types of tumors)
Testing positive for driver genes but not treated with TKIs
Tumor invasion of large blood vessels
central squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with cavitation
non-small cell lung cancer with hemoptysis (>5ml/day)
where the tumor is likely to invade important blood vessels and cause fatal bleeding during the subsequent study period
Accompanied by other types of malignant tumors within the past 5 years or currently
Planning to receive systemic anti-tumor therapy within 4 weeks before enrollment or during the study period
received extended-field radiation therapy (EF-RT) within 4 weeks before enrollment or limited-field radiation therapy within 2 weeks before enrollment
Unremitting toxic reactions caused by previous treatment, CTCAE grade >1, excluding hair loss
Various factors affecting oral medication (such as inability to swallow, gastrointestinal resection, chronic diarrhea, bowel obstruction)
Pleural effusion or ascites leading to respiratory syndrome (≥CTCAE grade 2)
Symptoms of brain metastasis not controlled and treated within 2 months
Presence of any severe or uncontrolled disease
Major surgery, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days before enrollment
Bleeding diathesis or history of significant bleeding, regardless of severity; any wound, ulcer, or fracture that has not healed following a bleeding or bleeding event (≥CTCAE grade 3)
Arterial/venous thrombosis within 6 months, such as cerebrovascular accident (including transient ischemic attack), venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism
History of substance abuse that cannot be quit
diagnosed with psychiatric disorders
Participated in other clinical trials of anti-tumor drugs within 4 weeks
Diagnosed with diseases that severely jeopardize patient safety or affect the completion of this study
Known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (i.e., HIV 1/2 antibody positive)
untreated active hepatitis B
active HCV infection

criteria.text: The patient must have histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
The patient must have progressive or recurrent NSCLC, and must have failed one and only one prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease.
The patient must not have received prior gemcitabine chemotherapy.
The patient must have measurable disease, as defined by RECIST, within 4 weeks prior to registration.
The patient must have an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
The patient must have a bilirubin level < 1.5 x upper limit of normal.
The patient must have an AST (SGOT) level < 3 x upper limit of normal.
The patient must have a serum creatinine level <= 1.5 mg/dL, or a calculated creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min.
The patient must have an absolute granulocyte count >= 1500/mm3 and a WBC >= 3000/mm^3.
The patient must have a hemoglobin level >= 9 g/L.
The patient must have a platelet count >= 100,000/mm^3.
The patient must have completed any radiation therapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration.
The patient must have completed prior cytotoxic chemotherapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration and have recovered from adverse effects from the chemotherapy to <= Grade 1, or baseline.
Patients with brain metastases which have been treated are eligible if the patient is > 3 weeks post completion of treatment for their brain metastases, and patient is neurologically stable.
Patients with previous brain metastases who have not yet received therapy specifically intended for their brain metastases are not eligible to enroll in this protocol.
The patient must have a life expectancy greater than 3 months.
Women must not be pregnant or breastfeeding.
A negative serum pregnancy test is required within 14 days of study entry.

Women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation.
HIV-positive patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy are excluded from the study.
The patient must not have an active second malignancy.

The patient must not have, at the time of registration, uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements.
The patient must not have a history of myocardial infarction within the prior 6 months.
The patient must not have symptomatic congestive heart failure.
The patient must not have unstable angina pectoris.
The patient must not have cardiac arrhythmia requiring medical intervention (with the exception of chronic, stable, asymptomatic atrial fibrillation).
The patient must not have pulmonary disease requiring oxygen.
The patient must not have dementia or active psychosis.
The patient must not have used any investigational agent in the month before study enrollment.
The patient must not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to Triapine® or other agents used in this study.
The patient must not have a clinical history of G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency.
Persons at high risk for G6PD deficiency (patients of African, Asian, or Mediterranean origin/ancestry) must undergo specific clinical testing at protocol entry for this condition.
Patients testing positive for G6PD deficiency are excluded from protocol entry.

transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "A Phase II Trial of Triapine (NSC #663249) in Combination With Gemcitabine as Second Line Treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a biopsy or other test that confirmed you have non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, a tissue biopsy confirmed my non-small cell lung cancer, not just cytology. By the way, I haven't used any investigational agents recently, I don't have G6PD deficiency, and I'd agree to use contraception during the study.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had progressive or recurrent NSCLC, and have you failed exactly one prior chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my cancer progressed and I failed exactly one prior chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease. The scans showed it growing again after that treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received gemcitabine chemotherapy in the past?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had gemcitabine. I'm ready for the next question.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any scans (like a CT or PET scan) within the last 4 weeks that showed measurable disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the specific timing of my scans. I know my cancer was growing again after the last chemo, but I don't recall if a scan was done within the last four weeks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us check eligibility, do you know if you had a CT or PET scan specifically in the last 4 weeks? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm still not sure about the exact date of my last scan, so I can't confirm if it was within the last four weeks. I know the cancer is active, but I don't have that specific record handy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To check your eligibility, do you know if your ECOG performance status is 0 or 1? This score measures how well you can perform ordinary tasks; 0 means fully active, and 1 means restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I would say my ECOG status is 0 or 1. I walk the dog every morning and do all my own housework, so I'm quite active.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm your ECOG status, do you have any trouble with self-care or daily activities, or are you fully independent?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I am fully independent with my self-care and daily activities. I walk the dog every morning and handle all my own housework without any trouble.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you completed any radiation therapy for your cancer? If so, was it at least 3 weeks before you would register for this study?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you completed any prior chemotherapy for your cancer? If so, was it at least 3 weeks ago, and have you recovered from any side effects to a mild level (Grade 1) or your normal baseline?

transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, have you fully recovered from the side effects of your last chemotherapy to a mild level (Grade 1) or your normal baseline?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I have fully recovered from the side effects and feel back to my normal baseline. I'm ready for the next question.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with brain metastases? If so, was it at least 3 weeks since the treatment finished, and have you been neurologically stable (no new or worsening symptoms) since then?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if I have brain metastases, so I'm not sure about that. I haven't mentioned it before, but I do know I don't have dementia or psychosis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for more than 3 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I certainly expect to live for more than 3 months. I'm still walking the dog and doing my housework, so I feel quite good.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not pregnant, and I am not breastfeeding either.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a blood or urine pregnancy test in the last 14 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I've had a pregnancy test in the last 14 days. I haven't had one recently, but I don't have the specific record to confirm the exact date.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to use effective birth control (like condoms or hormonal methods) or abstain from sex while in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.text: Are you currently taking combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV? (This is treatment for HIV. If you aren't sure or don't know, that's okay to say.)

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides my lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any active infections (like a fever or flu) or any mental health conditions that might make it hard to follow the study rules?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have any active infections like a fever or flu right now. As for mental health, I don't have dementia or psychosis, so I should be able to follow the rules just fine.

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart rhythm problem (cardiac arrhythmia) that required medical treatment? This excludes chronic, stable, and symptom-free atrial fibrillation. If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with a heart rhythm problem that required treatment. My heart seems to be working just fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently use oxygen therapy for any lung or breathing conditions?

transcript.text: No, I do not need oxygen for my lungs. I'm quite active and don't have any breathing issues that require that kind of support.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you taken part in any other clinical trials or received any investigational medications in the last month?

transcript.text: No, I have not taken part in any other clinical trials or received any investigational medications in the last month. I mentioned earlier that I haven't used any investigational agents recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to Triapine or any other medications used in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I came out in a rash once with an antibiotic, but I don't remember which one. I don't recall having any specific allergic reactions to Triapine or the other study medications.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us plan for the required G6PD testing, could you share if you have African, Asian, or Mediterranean ancestry?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "A Phase II Trial of Triapine (NSC #663249) in Combination With Gemcitabine as Second Line Treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer". transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a biopsy or other test that confirmed you have non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received exactly one prior chemotherapy treatment for your advanced lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, just the one chemotherapy regimen for the advanced cancer, and it failed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received a chemotherapy drug called gemcitabine?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Actually, I had two different chemotherapy regimens for the advanced cancer. But no, I have never received gemcitabine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any imaging scans (like a CT or PET scan) within the last 4 weeks to check if your cancer is still measurable?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the exact timing of my last scan. I know I finished my chemotherapy four weeks ago, but I don't recall if I had a scan right then.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, did you have a CT or PET scan specifically within the last 4 weeks to check your cancer size?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, wait, my last chemotherapy was only last week. I'm not sure about the exact timing of my last scan, but I don't recall having one specifically within the last 4 weeks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand your current health, how would you describe your ability to carry out daily activities? For example, are you fully active, or do you need some rest during the day?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm fully active. I work as a delivery driver, so I'm on my feet all day.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you completed any radiation therapy for your cancer? If so, was it at least 3 weeks ago?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: My radiation therapy finished one week ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Regarding your brain metastases treatment, are you currently experiencing any new or worsening neurological symptoms, such as headaches, vision changes, or weakness?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any headaches or vision changes. My brain is fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any specific treatment for your brain metastases?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't received any specific treatment for brain metastases. I don't have any history of them.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on your current health, do you expect to live for more than 3 months? It's okay if you're not sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I expect to live for more than 3 months. I'm feeling okay and ready to get back to work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am a man, so I am not pregnant. I am not breastfeeding either.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you are male, this criterion does not apply to you. Is there anything else you'd like to ask?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any other questions right now. I'm ready for the next step.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Even though you are male, the study requires a negative serum pregnancy test within 14 days of starting. Have you had this test done recently?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm a man, so I don't need a pregnancy test. I'm not sure what that means for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, are you currently using any form of birth control (like condoms or hormonal methods) or practicing abstinence to prevent pregnancy?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking combination antiretroviral therapy (HIV medication)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am HIV negative.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any other active cancer diagnosis besides lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any other active cancer diagnoses besides my lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any ongoing infections or other active health issues, such as uncontrolled psychiatric conditions, that might make it hard to follow the study rules?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any ongoing infections or other active health issues. My heart is fine as far as I know.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a heart attack in the last 6 months?

transcript.text: No, I haven't had a heart attack. My heart is fine as far as I know.

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with symptomatic congestive heart failure? (This means heart failure that causes symptoms like shortness of breath or swelling.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with congestive heart failure. My heart is fine as far as I know.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with unstable angina pectoris? (This is a type of chest pain that happens at rest or is getting worse.)

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart rhythm problem (arrhythmia) that required treatment? This excludes chronic, stable, and symptom-free atrial fibrillation.

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to Triapine or any other drugs with a similar chemical structure?

transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have African, Asian, or Mediterranean ancestry?

transcript.speaker: participant

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you aren't sure about your ancestry, would you be willing to have a simple blood test to check your G6PD levels? This test checks for the enzyme deficiency we discussed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, are you willing to have the blood test to check your G6PD levels?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm willing to have the blood test. I don't have any issues with blood tests.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

criteria.text: The patient must have histologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
The patient must have progressive or recurrent NSCLC, and must have failed one and only one prior cytotoxic chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease.
The patient must not have received prior gemcitabine chemotherapy.
The patient must have measurable disease, as defined by RECIST, within 4 weeks prior to registration.
The patient must have an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1.
The patient must have a bilirubin level < 1.5 x upper limit of normal.
The patient must have an AST (SGOT) level < 3 x upper limit of normal.
The patient must have a serum creatinine level <= 1.5 mg/dL, or a calculated creatinine clearance >= 60 mL/min.
The patient must have an absolute granulocyte count >= 1500/mm3 and a WBC >= 3000/mm^3.
The patient must have a hemoglobin level >= 9 g/L.
The patient must have a platelet count >= 100,000/mm^3.
The patient must have completed any radiation therapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration.
The patient must have completed prior cytotoxic chemotherapy >= 3 weeks prior to registration and have recovered from adverse effects from the chemotherapy to <= Grade 1, or baseline.
Patients with brain metastases which have been treated are eligible if the patient is > 3 weeks post completion of treatment for their brain metastases, and patient is neurologically stable.
Patients with previous brain metastases who have not yet received therapy specifically intended for their brain metastases are not eligible to enroll in this protocol.
The patient must have a life expectancy greater than 3 months.
Women must not be pregnant or breastfeeding.
A negative serum pregnancy test is required within 14 days of study entry.

Women of child-bearing potential and men must agree to use adequate contraception (hormonal or barrier method of birth control; abstinence) prior to study entry and for the duration of study participation.
HIV-positive patients receiving combination antiretroviral therapy are excluded from the study.
The patient must not have an active second malignancy.

The patient must not have, at the time of registration, uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements.
The patient must not have a history of myocardial infarction within the prior 6 months.
The patient must not have symptomatic congestive heart failure.
The patient must not have unstable angina pectoris.
The patient must not have cardiac arrhythmia requiring medical intervention (with the exception of chronic, stable, asymptomatic atrial fibrillation).
The patient must not have pulmonary disease requiring oxygen.
The patient must not have dementia or active psychosis.
The patient must not have used any investigational agent in the month before study enrollment.
The patient must not have a history of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to Triapine® or other agents used in this study.
The patient must not have a clinical history of G6PD (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) deficiency.
Persons at high risk for G6PD deficiency (patients of African, Asian, or Mediterranean origin/ancestry) must undergo specific clinical testing at protocol entry for this condition.
Patients testing positive for G6PD deficiency are excluded from protocol entry.

criteria.text: The participant is male or female and is 18 years of age or older.

The participant has histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on a biopsy performed within the last 90 days, or has a prior biopsy showing NSCLC if the current biopsy is deferred due to unacceptable safety risk.
The participant has a documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples tested by a CLIA-approved test.

If the participant was previously treated with osimertinib or another EGFR TKI, they must have received no more than 28 days of treatment and have no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment-related adverse events.
The participant has a PET-CT scan within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer.
The participant has a brain MRI (or CT if MRI is contraindicated) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease.
The participant is documented as a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon.
The participant has a tumor size of at least 1 centimeter in its longest diameter.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0-1.

The participant has no unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than CTCAE grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinum therapy-related neuropathy.
The participant's aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are less than or equal to 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN).

The participant's bilirubin level is less than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), or if they have documented Gilbert's syndrome, their conjugated bilirubin is within the normal range.
The participant's potassium and magnesium levels are within the normal range.
The participant's leukocyte count is greater than 3,000/microliter.
The participant's hemoglobin level is at least 9 g/dL, and they have not received a blood transfusion in the 28 days prior to study entry.
The participant's absolute neutrophil count is greater than 1,500/mcL.
The participant's platelet count is greater than 100,000/mcL.
For patients with serum creatinine > 1.5 x ULN, the creatinine clearance (CrCl) must be > 50 mL/min.
The participant has the ability to swallow oral medications.

Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment and agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib.
Definition: Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP) are women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation.
Definition: Women NOT of childbearing potential are women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal.
Definition: Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, and/or bilateral salpingectomy, but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion.
Management rule: Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP.

Definition: Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause. Women under 50 years old must be amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments with LH and FSH levels in the postmenopausal range. Women over 50 years of age must be amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments.

Acceptable contraception methods include total sexual abstinence, vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom, tubal occlusion plus male condom, copper-banded IUD plus male condom, levonorgestrel IUS plus male condom, medroxyprogesterone injections plus male condom, etonogestrel implants plus male condom, normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills plus male condom, norelgestromin/ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom, intravaginal device plus male condom, and Cerazette plus male condom.

Unacceptable contraception methods include triphasic combined oral contraceptives, all progesterone only pills except Cerazette, all barrier methods if used alone, non-copper containing intra-uterine devices, fertility awareness methods, and coitus interruptus.

Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have had a prior vasectomy or agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to administration of the first dose of study treatment, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib.
The participant does not have leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases.
The participant does not have Stage IIIB or distant metastases (including malignant pleural effusion) identified on PET-CT scan or biopsy.

The participant does not have a past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease.
The participant is not known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

The participant does not have an active second malignancy. Patients with a history of malignancy that has been completely treated, with no evidence of that cancer currently, are permitted to enroll provided all chemotherapy for prior malignancy was completed > 12 months prior and/or bone marrow transplant > 2 years prior.

The participant is not currently receiving treatment with contraindicated QTc prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers that cannot be discontinued or switched prior to the first day of study treatment, and tries to avoid concomitant use of any medications, herbal supplements, or foods with known inducer effects.

The participant does not have any of the following cardiac abnormalities or history: mean resting QTc > 470 msec, clinically important abnormalities in rhythm/conduction/morphology of resting ECG, or factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or arrhythmic events.

The participant has not received treatment with prohibited medications (concurrent anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal treatment [except corticosteroids and megesterolacetate], or immunotherapy) within 14 days prior to treatment with osimertinib.

The participant does not have any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension and active bleeding diatheses, which in the investigator's opinion makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the trial or which would jeopardize compliance with the protocol, or known active infection including chronic active hepatitis B, hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) with negative HBV viral load on appropriate antiviral therapy will be permitted, if able to continue appropriate antiviral therapy throughout treatment period.
The participant does not have active tuberculosis.
The participant does not have signs or symptoms of infection within 2 weeks prior to the first day of study.
The participant has not received therapeutic oral or intravenous (IV) antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to the first day of study treatment, except for prophylactic antibiotics.
The participant does not have Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system.

If the participant has known coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure not meeting the above criteria, or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50%, they must be on a stable medical regimen that is optimized in the opinion of the treating physician, in consultation with a cardiologist if appropriate.

The participant has not experienced untreated and/or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions and/or has not had symptomatic cardiac dysfunction (unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous 3 months; coronary angioplasty, or stenting or bypass grafting within the past 6 months; cardiac ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication; any history of second (2nd) or third (3rd) degree atrioventricular conduction defects).
Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding are excluded.

The participant does not have active gastrointestinal (GI) disease (including GI bleeding or ulceration) or other condition that could affect GI absorption (e.g. malabsorption syndrome, history of biliary tract disease), including refractory nausea or vomiting, or chronic GI disease which may affect absorption or tolerance to oral medications.
The participant does not have a history of hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of osimertinib or drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to osimertinib.
The participant is not involved in the planning and/or conduct of the study.
The participant has not participated in another clinical study with an investigational product during the last 2 months or within five half-lives of the compound, whichever is longer.

The participant does not have uncontrolled medical, psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that interfere with the patient's safety, ability to provide informed consent, or ability to comply with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "Osimertinib in Treating Participants With Stage I-IIIA EGFR-mutant Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Before Surgery". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 67 years old. I'm definitely old enough!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a biopsy that confirmed you have non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the last 90 days, or do you have a prior biopsy result showing NSCLC?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I had a biopsy two months ago that confirmed non-small cell lung cancer. I believe that's within the 90-day window, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, was that biopsy result from within the last 90 days? (Two months is roughly 60 days, which is within the window.) If you aren't sure of the exact date, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I'm sure it was two months ago, so that's about 60 days. That fits within the 90-day window, doesn't it?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a result from a CLIA-approved genetic test on your tumor sample that confirms an activating EGFR mutation (such as Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R)? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I know I have the lung cancer, but I don't recall anything about genetic tests or EGFR mutations.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you previously taken osimertinib or another EGFR TKI medication for your lung cancer? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't taken osimertinib or any other EGFR TKI medication. I haven't had any chemotherapy or radiation either, as I mentioned before.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a PET-CT scan within the last 60 days to check the stage of your lung cancer? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I forgot, I do take a heart rhythm tablet every day, my current treatment. I'm not sure if I've had a PET-CT scan within the last 60 days.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for letting me know. Have you had a brain MRI (or CT scan if MRI isn't possible) within the last 60 days to check for any spread of cancer to the brain? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I know I have the lung cancer, but I don't recall anything about brain scans or MRIs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been told by a thoracic surgeon (a surgeon who specializes in chest surgery) that you are a candidate for surgery to remove your lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I know I have the lung cancer, but I haven't spoken to a surgeon about removing it yet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your lung tumor is at least 1 centimeter in its longest size? If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the exact size of the tumor. I know I have the cancer, but I don't recall the specific measurements from my biopsy report.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you know if your ECOG Performance Status is 0 or 1? This score measures how well you can perform usual daily activities, where 0 means fully active and 1 means restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory. If you aren't sure, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I am out in the garden every day, so I feel quite active. I think that means my status is good, probably a 0 or 1.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you able to carry out all of your usual daily activities without any restrictions? (This would be an ECOG score of 0).

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can carry out all my usual daily activities without any restrictions. I'm quite active, as I mentioned, I'm out in the garden every day.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Since you mentioned you are quite active, do you currently have any side effects or health issues from previous cancer treatments that are still bothering you or haven't fully resolved? (This excludes hair loss or mild numbness in hands/feet from prior chemotherapy).

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any chemotherapy or radiation, so I don't have any side effects from those. I just take my heart rhythm tablet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you able to swallow oral medications, like your heart rhythm tablet, without difficulty?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I can swallow oral medications fine. I take my heart rhythm tablet every day without any trouble.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or could you become pregnant during the study? If so, are you willing to have a pregnancy test before starting treatment and use highly effective birth control during the study and for 90 days after the last dose?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not pregnant and I am not breastfeeding. I would agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days after the last dose.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to have a negative serum pregnancy test (a blood test) within 3 days before starting the study treatment?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't know if I can get a blood test done within three days before starting.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us plan, could you tell me which specific birth control method you are currently using or plan to use? For example, are you abstinent, or using a method like an IUD, implant, or pill?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I see. Since I am a woman, that question about men with female partners doesn't apply to me. I'm not sure what specific method I should use, to be honest.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us narrow down the options, do you currently use any birth control methods like pills, an IUD, or an implant? If not, are you open to using one of the acceptable methods listed in the study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure what specific methods are acceptable or if I use any right now. I just know I'm willing to agree to use highly effective contraception as needed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, are you currently using any birth control methods like pills, an IUD, or an implant? If so, do you know the specific name or type?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure if I'm currently using any specific birth control methods like pills or an IUD. I just know I'm willing to agree to use highly effective contraception as needed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (cancer in the fluid around the brain and spine) or other metastases in the central nervous system (CNS)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with that. I don't recall any issues with my brain or spine fluid.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told you have Stage IIIB lung cancer or cancer that has spread to other parts of your body (distant metastases), such as fluid around the lungs?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been told I have Stage IIIB or that it has spread. I just know I have the non-small cell lung cancer confirmed by biopsy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with interstitial lung disease (scarring in the lungs), had lung inflammation from radiation that required steroid treatment, or had lung issues caused by medications?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with interstitial lung disease or had lung inflammation from radiation or medications.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been tested and found to be positive for HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not HIV positive. I have never had that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides this lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with any other type of cancer besides this lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently taking any medications, herbal supplements, or foods that might affect your heart rhythm or interact with other drugs? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I forgot, I do take a heart rhythm tablet every day, my current treatment. I'm not sure if it interacts with other drugs, but that's the only medication I'm on.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Could you tell me the exact name of the heart rhythm tablet you take? I need to check if it's one that affects heart rhythm or interacts with other drugs.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I don't remember the exact name of the tablet. I just know it's for my heart rhythm.

transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told by a doctor that you have an abnormal heart rhythm, an abnormal ECG, or a condition that increases your risk for heart rhythm problems?

transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, have you ever had an ECG (heart tracing) that showed an abnormality in your heart's rhythm or electrical pattern?
