transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any severe, uncontrolled health conditions (like high blood pressure or active infections such as hepatitis or HIV) that a doctor has said might make it unsafe for you to join this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any severe, uncontrolled health conditions like high blood pressure or active infections. I just take my heart rhythm tablet, but I'm not sure if that counts as uncontrolled.

transcript.speaker: agent

criteria.text: The participant is male or female and is 18 years of age or older.

The participant has histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on a biopsy performed within the last 90 days, or has a prior biopsy showing NSCLC if the current biopsy is deferred due to unacceptable safety risk.
The participant has a documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples tested by a CLIA-approved test.

If the participant was previously treated with osimertinib or another EGFR TKI, they must have received no more than 28 days of treatment and have no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment-related adverse events.
The participant has a PET-CT scan within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer.
The participant has a brain MRI (or CT if MRI is contraindicated) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease.
The participant is documented as a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon.
The participant has a tumor size of at least 1 centimeter in its longest diameter.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0-1.

The participant has no unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than CTCAE grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinum therapy-related neuropathy.
The participant's aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are less than or equal to 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN).

The participant's bilirubin level is less than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), or if they have documented Gilbert's syndrome, their conjugated bilirubin is within the normal range.
The participant's potassium and magnesium levels are within the normal range.
The participant's leukocyte count is greater than 3,000/microliter.
The participant's hemoglobin level is at least 9 g/dL, and they have not received a blood transfusion in the 28 days prior to study entry.
The participant's absolute neutrophil count is greater than 1,500/mcL.
The participant's platelet count is greater than 100,000/mcL.
For patients with serum creatinine > 1.5 x ULN, the creatinine clearance (CrCl) must be > 50 mL/min.
The participant has the ability to swallow oral medications.

Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment and agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib.
Definition: Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP) are women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation.
Definition: Women NOT of childbearing potential are women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal.
Definition: Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, and/or bilateral salpingectomy, but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion.
Management rule: Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP.

Definition: Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause. Women under 50 years old must be amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments with LH and FSH levels in the postmenopausal range. Women over 50 years of age must be amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments.

Acceptable contraception methods include total sexual abstinence, vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom, tubal occlusion plus male condom, copper-banded IUD plus male condom, levonorgestrel IUS plus male condom, medroxyprogesterone injections plus male condom, etonogestrel implants plus male condom, normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills plus male condom, norelgestromin/ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom, intravaginal device plus male condom, and Cerazette plus male condom.

Unacceptable contraception methods include triphasic combined oral contraceptives, all progesterone only pills except Cerazette, all barrier methods if used alone, non-copper containing intra-uterine devices, fertility awareness methods, and coitus interruptus.

Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have had a prior vasectomy or agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to administration of the first dose of study treatment, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib.
The participant does not have leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases.
The participant does not have Stage IIIB or distant metastases (including malignant pleural effusion) identified on PET-CT scan or biopsy.

The participant does not have a past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease.
The participant is not known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

The participant does not have an active second malignancy. Patients with a history of malignancy that has been completely treated, with no evidence of that cancer currently, are permitted to enroll provided all chemotherapy for prior malignancy was completed > 12 months prior and/or bone marrow transplant > 2 years prior.

The participant is not currently receiving treatment with contraindicated QTc prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers that cannot be discontinued or switched prior to the first day of study treatment, and tries to avoid concomitant use of any medications, herbal supplements, or foods with known inducer effects.

The participant does not have any of the following cardiac abnormalities or history: mean resting QTc > 470 msec, clinically important abnormalities in rhythm/conduction/morphology of resting ECG, or factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or arrhythmic events.

The participant has not received treatment with prohibited medications (concurrent anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal treatment [except corticosteroids and megesterolacetate], or immunotherapy) within 14 days prior to treatment with osimertinib.

The participant does not have any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension and active bleeding diatheses, which in the investigator's opinion makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the trial or which would jeopardize compliance with the protocol, or known active infection including chronic active hepatitis B, hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) with negative HBV viral load on appropriate antiviral therapy will be permitted, if able to continue appropriate antiviral therapy throughout treatment period.
The participant does not have active tuberculosis.
The participant does not have signs or symptoms of infection within 2 weeks prior to the first day of study.
The participant has not received therapeutic oral or intravenous (IV) antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to the first day of study treatment, except for prophylactic antibiotics.
The participant does not have Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system.

If the participant has known coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure not meeting the above criteria, or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50%, they must be on a stable medical regimen that is optimized in the opinion of the treating physician, in consultation with a cardiologist if appropriate.

The participant has not experienced untreated and/or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions and/or has not had symptomatic cardiac dysfunction (unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous 3 months; coronary angioplasty, or stenting or bypass grafting within the past 6 months; cardiac ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication; any history of second (2nd) or third (3rd) degree atrioventricular conduction defects).
Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding are excluded.

The participant does not have active gastrointestinal (GI) disease (including GI bleeding or ulceration) or other condition that could affect GI absorption (e.g. malabsorption syndrome, history of biliary tract disease), including refractory nausea or vomiting, or chronic GI disease which may affect absorption or tolerance to oral medications.
The participant does not have a history of hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of osimertinib or drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to osimertinib.
The participant is not involved in the planning and/or conduct of the study.
The participant has not participated in another clinical study with an investigational product during the last 2 months or within five half-lives of the compound, whichever is longer.

The participant does not have uncontrolled medical, psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that interfere with the patient's safety, ability to provide informed consent, or ability to comply with the protocol.

criteria.text: The participant is male or female and is 18 years of age or older.

The participant has histologically or cytologically confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) based on a biopsy performed within the last 90 days, or has a prior biopsy showing NSCLC if the current biopsy is deferred due to unacceptable safety risk.
The participant has a documented activating EGFR mutation (Exon 19 deletion, T790M, or L858R) on tumor samples tested by a CLIA-approved test.

If the participant was previously treated with osimertinib or another EGFR TKI, they must have received no more than 28 days of treatment and have no evidence of grade 2 or greater treatment-related adverse events.
The participant has a PET-CT scan within the last 60 days showing radiographic stage I to IIIa lung cancer.
The participant has a brain MRI (or CT if MRI is contraindicated) within the last 60 days showing no evidence of metastatic disease.
The participant is documented as a candidate for surgical resection of their lung cancer by an American Board of Thoracic Surgery certified surgeon.
The participant has a tumor size of at least 1 centimeter in its longest diameter.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0-1.

The participant has no unresolved toxicities from prior therapy greater than CTCAE grade 1 at the time of starting study treatment, with the exception of alopecia and grade 2 prior platinum therapy-related neuropathy.
The participant's aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels are less than or equal to 2.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN).

The participant's bilirubin level is less than or equal to 1.5 times the upper limit of normal (ULN), or if they have documented Gilbert's syndrome, their conjugated bilirubin is within the normal range.
The participant's potassium and magnesium levels are within the normal range.
The participant's leukocyte count is greater than 3,000/microliter.
The participant's hemoglobin level is at least 9 g/dL, and they have not received a blood transfusion in the 28 days prior to study entry.
The participant's absolute neutrophil count is greater than 1,500/mcL.
The participant's platelet count is greater than 100,000/mcL.
For patients with serum creatinine > 1.5 x ULN, the creatinine clearance (CrCl) must be > 50 mL/min.
The participant has the ability to swallow oral medications.

Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 3 days prior to the first dose of study treatment and agree to use highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib.
Definition: Women of childbearing potential (WoCBP) are women between menarche and menopause who have not been permanently or surgically sterilized and are capable of procreation.
Definition: Women NOT of childbearing potential are women who are permanently or surgically sterilized or postmenopausal.
Definition: Permanent sterilization includes hysterectomy, bilateral oophorectomy, and/or bilateral salpingectomy, but excludes bilateral tubal occlusion.
Management rule: Women who have undergone tubal occlusion should be managed on trials as if they are of WoCBP.

Definition: Women will be considered postmenopausal if they are amenorrhoeic for 12 months without an alternative medical cause. Women under 50 years old must be amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of exogenous hormonal treatments with LH and FSH levels in the postmenopausal range. Women over 50 years of age must be amenorrhoeic for 12 months or more following cessation of all exogenous hormonal treatments.

Acceptable contraception methods include total sexual abstinence, vasectomized sexual partner plus male condom, tubal occlusion plus male condom, copper-banded IUD plus male condom, levonorgestrel IUS plus male condom, medroxyprogesterone injections plus male condom, etonogestrel implants plus male condom, normal and low dose combined oral contraceptive pills plus male condom, norelgestromin/ethinylestradiol transdermal system plus male condom, intravaginal device plus male condom, and Cerazette plus male condom.

Unacceptable contraception methods include triphasic combined oral contraceptives, all progesterone only pills except Cerazette, all barrier methods if used alone, non-copper containing intra-uterine devices, fertility awareness methods, and coitus interruptus.

Men with a female partner of childbearing potential must have had a prior vasectomy or agree to use effective contraception as described in the full protocol for at least 14 days prior to administration of the first dose of study treatment, during the study, and for 90 days following the last dose of osimertinib.
The participant does not have leptomeningeal carcinomatosis or other central nervous system (CNS) metastases.
The participant does not have Stage IIIB or distant metastases (including malignant pleural effusion) identified on PET-CT scan or biopsy.

The participant does not have a past medical history of interstitial lung disease, drug-induced interstitial lung disease, radiation pneumonitis which required steroid treatment, or any evidence of clinically active interstitial lung disease.
The participant is not known to be serologically positive for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

The participant does not have an active second malignancy. Patients with a history of malignancy that has been completely treated, with no evidence of that cancer currently, are permitted to enroll provided all chemotherapy for prior malignancy was completed > 12 months prior and/or bone marrow transplant > 2 years prior.

The participant is not currently receiving treatment with contraindicated QTc prolonging medications or potent CYP3A4 inducers that cannot be discontinued or switched prior to the first day of study treatment, and tries to avoid concomitant use of any medications, herbal supplements, or foods with known inducer effects.

The participant does not have any of the following cardiac abnormalities or history: mean resting QTc > 470 msec, clinically important abnormalities in rhythm/conduction/morphology of resting ECG, or factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or arrhythmic events.

The participant has not received treatment with prohibited medications (concurrent anticancer therapy including chemotherapy, radiation, hormonal treatment [except corticosteroids and megesterolacetate], or immunotherapy) within 14 days prior to treatment with osimertinib.

The participant does not have any evidence of severe or uncontrolled systemic diseases, including uncontrolled hypertension and active bleeding diatheses, which in the investigator's opinion makes it undesirable for the patient to participate in the trial or which would jeopardize compliance with the protocol, or known active infection including chronic active hepatitis B, hepatitis C and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) with negative HBV viral load on appropriate antiviral therapy will be permitted, if able to continue appropriate antiviral therapy throughout treatment period.
The participant does not have active tuberculosis.
The participant does not have signs or symptoms of infection within 2 weeks prior to the first day of study.
The participant has not received therapeutic oral or intravenous (IV) antibiotics within 2 weeks prior to the first day of study treatment, except for prophylactic antibiotics.
The participant does not have Class II to IV heart failure as defined by the New York Heart Association functional classification system.

If the participant has known coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure not meeting the above criteria, or left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) < 50%, they must be on a stable medical regimen that is optimized in the opinion of the treating physician, in consultation with a cardiologist if appropriate.

The participant has not experienced untreated and/or uncontrolled cardiovascular conditions and/or has not had symptomatic cardiac dysfunction (unstable angina, congestive heart failure, myocardial infarction within the previous 3 months; coronary angioplasty, or stenting or bypass grafting within the past 6 months; cardiac ventricular arrhythmias requiring medication; any history of second (2nd) or third (3rd) degree atrioventricular conduction defects).
Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding are excluded.

The participant does not have active gastrointestinal (GI) disease (including GI bleeding or ulceration) or other condition that could affect GI absorption (e.g. malabsorption syndrome, history of biliary tract disease), including refractory nausea or vomiting, or chronic GI disease which may affect absorption or tolerance to oral medications.
The participant does not have a history of hypersensitivity to active or inactive excipients of osimertinib or drugs with a similar chemical structure or class to osimertinib.
The participant is not involved in the planning and/or conduct of the study.
The participant has not participated in another clinical study with an investigational product during the last 2 months or within five half-lives of the compound, whichever is longer.

The participant does not have uncontrolled medical, psychological, familial, sociological, or geographical conditions that interfere with the patient's safety, ability to provide informed consent, or ability to comply with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "Osimertinib in Treating Participants With Stage I-IIIA EGFR-mutant Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Before Surgery". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 74 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a biopsy that confirmed you have non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in the last 90 days, or do you have a prior biopsy result for NSCLC?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't recall having a biopsy for lung cancer recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: To clarify, have you ever had a biopsy (a small tissue sample) that confirmed you have non-small cell lung cancer, even if it was a while ago?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't think so. I've never been told I have lung cancer, and I don't recall any biopsies for it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever had a tumor sample tested for an EGFR mutation (a specific genetic change in the cancer cells)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I've never been told I have cancer, so I wouldn't know if my tumor was tested for anything like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a PET-CT scan in the last 60 days? This is a special imaging test that helps doctors see the stage of the cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "A Trial of SHR-1316/Placebo in Combination With Chemotherapy in Patients With Resectable NSCLC". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have an ECOG performance status of 0 or 1? This score measures how well you can perform usual daily activities. If you aren't sure of your exact score, that's okay—just let me know.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm a retired farmer, so I'm still out working in the fields most days. I'd say I'm doing pretty well, but I'm not sure what that 'ECOG' score is exactly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help clarify, are you able to carry out all of your usual daily activities, including working in the fields, without any restrictions?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh yes, I can still do all my usual chores around the farm. I might not be as fast as I used to be, but I don't have any restrictions stopping me from working.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you been diagnosed with Stage II, IIIA, or Selected IIIB Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) that is considered resectable (able to be removed with surgery)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Well, I did have some lung trouble a few years back that the doctor called inflammation, but I don't recall being told it was cancer or that it needed surgery. I'm not sure if that counts.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks for clarifying. Have you had a thoracic surgeon evaluate you and confirm that your lung condition can be completely removed with surgery with the goal of curing it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I haven't seen a thoracic surgeon for that. I just saw my regular doctor for the inflammation a while back. I don't know if that counts.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent scans (like a CT or PET scan) where your doctor said they could clearly see and measure the size of the lung tumor?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about any recent scans or tumors. I just know I had that inflammation a while back, but I haven't had any new tests for it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, have you had any recent imaging tests (like a CT or PET scan) where your doctor identified a specific tumor or lesion that could be measured?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any of those scans. Like I said, I just know about the inflammation from a few years ago, but I don't have any recent tests showing a tumor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any recent blood tests (like within the last 2 weeks) to check your liver, kidney, and bone marrow function?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about recent blood tests. I haven't had any new tests for my lungs, so I doubt I've had blood work done for that recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently using any form of birth control, or are you abstinent from sexual activity?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm a 70-year-old man, so I don't use birth control. I'm married, but we've been past that stage of life for a long time now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received any systemic anti-cancer treatments (such as chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy) specifically for lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I think they gave me something through a drip a while back, but I am not sure what it was for. It might have been for something else entirely.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, was the treatment you received through a drip specifically for lung cancer, or was it for a different condition?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I really can't say for sure. I know I had that drip, but I don't remember if it was for the lung inflammation or something else entirely. It's been a long time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any known autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or psoriasis?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about any of those fancy names like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis. I just know I had that lung inflammation a while back, but I haven't been told I have any of those other autoimmune diseases.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be clear, have you ever been diagnosed with an autoimmune disease (where your immune system attacks your own body), such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or psoriasis?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with any of those autoimmune diseases. I just had that lung inflammation a while back, but nothing else like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other type of cancer (malignancy) besides Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) in the last 5 years?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any other cancers besides that lung trouble. I'm just a simple farmer, so I don't think I've had anything else like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with pneumonitis, interstitial lung disease, or any other severe lung conditions that might affect how your lungs work?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Well, the doctor did call it inflammation a few years back, so I guess that counts as some kind of lung trouble. I'm not sure if it was exactly what you're calling pneumonitis, but my lungs have had issues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us understand better, did a doctor ever tell you that you had a condition called pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know if the doctor used those specific words, but he did say my lungs were inflamed. I'm not sure if that's the same thing as pneumonitis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a significant heart or blood vessel condition, such as a heart attack, stroke, or heart failure?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any heart attacks or strokes. I feel pretty good otherwise, just a bit older than I used to be.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Aside from heart attacks and strokes, have you ever been diagnosed with other significant heart or blood vessel conditions, such as heart failure, angina, or peripheral artery disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had heart failure or angina either. I'm just a simple farmer with some lung trouble, but my heart seems fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a significant bleeding disorder, such as hemophilia or von Willebrand disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never heard of those bleeding disorders. I'm just a simple farmer, and I don't recall ever having trouble with bleeding more than usual.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, have you ever been diagnosed with a bleeding disorder like hemophilia or von Willebrand disease, or do you take blood thinners like warfarin or apixaban?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I've never been diagnosed with a bleeding disorder, and I don't take any blood thinners. I'm just a simple farmer who likes to stay active.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a blood clot in an artery or vein, such as a deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or a pulmonary embolism (PE)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any blood clots like that. I've had some lung inflammation, but no clots in my veins or lungs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been diagnosed with HIV. I've had my ups and downs with drinking in the past, but I've been clean for years now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with Hepatitis B or Hepatitis C (liver infections caused by viruses)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had hepatitis B or hepatitis C. I've had my ups and downs with drinking in the past, but I've been clean for years now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had an allergic reaction to monoclonal antibodies or other protein drugs?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never been allergic to any drugs, antibody ones included. I've had my ups and downs with drinking in the past, but I've been clean for years now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently allergic to SHR-1316 or any of the chemotherapy drugs used in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have never had an allergic reaction to any medicine. I'm just a simple farmer, and I don't recall ever having trouble with allergies to drugs.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently pregnant or breastfeeding?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Me? No, I am not pregnant. And I certainly am not lactating, being a 70-year-old man. I think we've covered the family planning stuff, haven't we?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any current or past diagnoses of psychiatric conditions or substance use disorders?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I used to drink too much, years back, but not so much now. I don't have any other psychiatric issues, just the old drinking habit.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, have you had any issues with alcohol or drug use in the past 12 months?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any issues with drinking or drugs in the last year. I've been clean for quite a while now, just tending to my farm.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had a confirmed or suspected COVID-19 infection, or been a close contact with someone who has or is suspected to have it, recently?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Hard to say. There was a bug going round at church, it could have been COVID. I don't know for sure if I was exposed.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To be sure, have you ever tested positive for COVID-19, or been in close contact with someone who has or had it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't think I've ever tested positive for it, but I can't say for sure if I was around someone who had it. It's been a while, and I'm not keeping track of every bug at church.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

criteria.text: Patient must be capable of giving signed informed consent, including mandatory genetic informed consent and compliance with ICF and protocol requirements.
Signed and dated written ICFs must be provided prior to any mandatory study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses.
Patients must provide signed and dated written optional genetic informed consent prior to collection of a sample for optional genetic analysis at the time of second screening.
ICF1 must be signed and dated prior to any study procedures and prior to the planned surgical resection of the primary NSCLC.
Age ≥18 years at the time of screening.
Male and/or female.
Diagnosis of histologically confirmed NSCLC (WHO 2015 classification) with resectable (stage II-III) disease (according to IASLC Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology v8.0).
Select (ie, T3N2 or T4N2) stage IIIB patients will be eligible, provided that they are upstaged to T3N2 or T4N2 based on confirmed pathology.
Patients who are staged as T3N2 or T4N2 prior to surgery are not eligible.
A contrast-enhanced CT or MRI scan of the chest must have been done for surgical planning prior to surgery.
Complete resection of the primary NSCLC is mandatory.
Patients undergoing wedge resection are not eligible for this study.
Patients undergoing segmentectomy must have tumors less than 2 cm in maximum diameter.

Where a resection has been extended by means of a wedge resection of an adjacent lobe to ensure complete resection of a tumor at or crossing a fissure between lobes, this is acceptable if surgical margins are clear of disease.
Where the resection of a second tumor nodule (eg, a T4 lesion) is undertaken by means of a wedge resection of a separate lobe, then the patient is not eligible.
The surgeon performing the resection should remove all gross disease by the end of surgery.
All surgical margins of resection must be macroscopically negative for tumor.

Pathology and/or operative reports must include the examination of at least 2 different mediastinal lymph node (N2) levels, one of which is the subcarinal node-group (level 7) and the second of which is lobe-specific.
No extracapsular nodal extension of the tumor is observed in resected mediastinal N2 lymph nodes.
All patients who enrol in the study prior to surgery must have a pre-surgical plasma sample collected for MRD evaluation.
Confirmation of suitable samples of resected tumor tissue and whole blood for WES of tumor and germline DNA, respectively, and creation of Sponsor-approved personalized panel for MRD detection.
Germline sequencing of whole blood is mandatory.
If a patient's tumor has less than the requisite 50 tumor-specific variants, a panel cannot be built and the patient will no longer be able to participate in the study.
Established MRD status (MRD+ or MRD-) based on Sponsor-approved personalized assay of a plasma sample collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery.
Known tumor PD-L1 status determined at a central reference laboratory testing service using a validated Ventana SP263 PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay prior randomization.
Patients with unknown PD-L1 status are not eligible for the study.
Post-operative CT scan of the chest (including liver and adrenal glands) performed within 28 days + 7 days prior to randomization.
ICF2 must be signed and dated after MRD status is determined and prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses outlined in SoAs in Table 2 and Table 3.
Randomization must occur within the 12 weeks (+ 7 days) following surgery.
WHO/Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

Complete postoperative wound healing must have occurred prior to randomization; patients must have recovered from all acute, reversible toxic effects from prior treatments (excluding alopecia) that could potentially adversely impact further administration of durvalumab/placebo or chemotherapy according to the Investigator's judgment.
Eligible to tolerate 4 cycles of platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy
Adequate organ and marrow function as described in the protocol.
Must have a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
Body weight >30 kg
Post-operative imaging demonstrating unequivocal evidence of disease recurrence or tissue biopsy-proven disease recurrence.
EGFR-mutant and/or ALK-translocation-positive, as assessed either from a pre-surgical biopsy sample (preferred) or the resected tumor tissue (if biopsy was not evaluable or available).
Mixed small cell and NSCLC histology.

Require re-resection or are deemed to have unresectable NSCLC by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients who are candidates to undergo only wedge resections.
History of allogeneic organ or bone marrow transplantation.
Non-leukocyte-depleted whole blood transfusion within 120 days of genetic sample collection.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease [eg, colitis or Crohn's disease], diverticulitis [with the exception of diverticulosis], systemic lupus erythematosus, Sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome [granulomatosis with polyangiitis, Graves' disease, rheumatoid arthritis, hypophysitis, uveitis, etc]).

Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, active ILD, serious chronic gastrointestinal conditions associated with diarrhea, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, substantially increase risk of incurring AEs, or compromise the ability of the patient to give written informed consent.
History of another primary malignancy, except for
History of active primary immunodeficiency

Active infection, including tuberculosis (clinical evaluation that includes clinical history, physical examination, and radiographic findings, and tuberculosis testing in line with local practice), hepatitis B (HBV; known positive HBV surface antigen [HBsAg] result), hepatitis C (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus infection (positive HIV 1/2 antibodies).
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the IPs or any of the IP excipients.
Any medical contraindication to treatment with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as listed in the local labeling.
Received any prior adjuvant therapy for NSCLC or any prior exposure to durvalumab.
Any concurrent chemotherapy, IP, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.
Radiotherapy treatment for NSCLC in the neoadjuvant setting.
Radiotherapy treatment to more than 30% of the bone marrow or with a wide field of radiation within 4 weeks of the first dose of IP.
Receipt of live attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Major surgical procedure (as defined by the Investigator) within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Participation in another clinical study with an IP administered since completion of surgery.
Previous IP assignment in the present study.
Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (noninterventional) clinical study, or during the follow-up period of an interventional study.
Prior randomization or treatment in a previous durvalumab clinical study regardless of treatment group assignment.
Patients who are never-smokers; defined as no more than 100 cigarettes or its equivalent in his/her lifetime.

Female patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding or male or female patients of reproductive potential who are not willing to employ effective birth control from screening to 90 days after the last dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Judgment by the Investigator that the patient should not participate in the study if the patient is unlikely to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements.

criteria.text: Patient must be capable of giving signed informed consent, including mandatory genetic informed consent and compliance with ICF and protocol requirements.
Signed and dated written ICFs must be provided prior to any mandatory study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses.
Patients must provide signed and dated written optional genetic informed consent prior to collection of a sample for optional genetic analysis at the time of second screening.
ICF1 must be signed and dated prior to any study procedures and prior to the planned surgical resection of the primary NSCLC.
Age ≥18 years at the time of screening.
Male and/or female.
Diagnosis of histologically confirmed NSCLC (WHO 2015 classification) with resectable (stage II-III) disease (according to IASLC Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology v8.0).
Select (ie, T3N2 or T4N2) stage IIIB patients will be eligible, provided that they are upstaged to T3N2 or T4N2 based on confirmed pathology.
Patients who are staged as T3N2 or T4N2 prior to surgery are not eligible.
A contrast-enhanced CT or MRI scan of the chest must have been done for surgical planning prior to surgery.
Complete resection of the primary NSCLC is mandatory.
Patients undergoing wedge resection are not eligible for this study.
Patients undergoing segmentectomy must have tumors less than 2 cm in maximum diameter.

Where a resection has been extended by means of a wedge resection of an adjacent lobe to ensure complete resection of a tumor at or crossing a fissure between lobes, this is acceptable if surgical margins are clear of disease.
Where the resection of a second tumor nodule (eg, a T4 lesion) is undertaken by means of a wedge resection of a separate lobe, then the patient is not eligible.
The surgeon performing the resection should remove all gross disease by the end of surgery.
All surgical margins of resection must be macroscopically negative for tumor.

Pathology and/or operative reports must include the examination of at least 2 different mediastinal lymph node (N2) levels, one of which is the subcarinal node-group (level 7) and the second of which is lobe-specific.
No extracapsular nodal extension of the tumor is observed in resected mediastinal N2 lymph nodes.
All patients who enrol in the study prior to surgery must have a pre-surgical plasma sample collected for MRD evaluation.
Confirmation of suitable samples of resected tumor tissue and whole blood for WES of tumor and germline DNA, respectively, and creation of Sponsor-approved personalized panel for MRD detection.
Germline sequencing of whole blood is mandatory.
If a patient's tumor has less than the requisite 50 tumor-specific variants, a panel cannot be built and the patient will no longer be able to participate in the study.
Established MRD status (MRD+ or MRD-) based on Sponsor-approved personalized assay of a plasma sample collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery.
Known tumor PD-L1 status determined at a central reference laboratory testing service using a validated Ventana SP263 PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay prior randomization.
Patients with unknown PD-L1 status are not eligible for the study.
Post-operative CT scan of the chest (including liver and adrenal glands) performed within 28 days + 7 days prior to randomization.
ICF2 must be signed and dated after MRD status is determined and prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses outlined in SoAs in Table 2 and Table 3.
Randomization must occur within the 12 weeks (+ 7 days) following surgery.
WHO/Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

Complete postoperative wound healing must have occurred prior to randomization; patients must have recovered from all acute, reversible toxic effects from prior treatments (excluding alopecia) that could potentially adversely impact further administration of durvalumab/placebo or chemotherapy according to the Investigator's judgment.
Eligible to tolerate 4 cycles of platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy
Adequate organ and marrow function as described in the protocol.
Must have a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
Body weight >30 kg
Post-operative imaging demonstrating unequivocal evidence of disease recurrence or tissue biopsy-proven disease recurrence.
EGFR-mutant and/or ALK-translocation-positive, as assessed either from a pre-surgical biopsy sample (preferred) or the resected tumor tissue (if biopsy was not evaluable or available).
Mixed small cell and NSCLC histology.

Require re-resection or are deemed to have unresectable NSCLC by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients who are candidates to undergo only wedge resections.
History of allogeneic organ or bone marrow transplantation.
Non-leukocyte-depleted whole blood transfusion within 120 days of genetic sample collection.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease [eg, colitis or Crohn's disease], diverticulitis [with the exception of diverticulosis], systemic lupus erythematosus, Sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome [granulomatosis with polyangiitis, Graves' disease, rheumatoid arthritis, hypophysitis, uveitis, etc]).

Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, active ILD, serious chronic gastrointestinal conditions associated with diarrhea, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, substantially increase risk of incurring AEs, or compromise the ability of the patient to give written informed consent.
History of another primary malignancy, except for
History of active primary immunodeficiency

Active infection, including tuberculosis (clinical evaluation that includes clinical history, physical examination, and radiographic findings, and tuberculosis testing in line with local practice), hepatitis B (HBV; known positive HBV surface antigen [HBsAg] result), hepatitis C (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus infection (positive HIV 1/2 antibodies).
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the IPs or any of the IP excipients.
Any medical contraindication to treatment with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as listed in the local labeling.
Received any prior adjuvant therapy for NSCLC or any prior exposure to durvalumab.
Any concurrent chemotherapy, IP, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.
Radiotherapy treatment for NSCLC in the neoadjuvant setting.
Radiotherapy treatment to more than 30% of the bone marrow or with a wide field of radiation within 4 weeks of the first dose of IP.
Receipt of live attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Major surgical procedure (as defined by the Investigator) within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Participation in another clinical study with an IP administered since completion of surgery.
Previous IP assignment in the present study.
Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (noninterventional) clinical study, or during the follow-up period of an interventional study.
Prior randomization or treatment in a previous durvalumab clinical study regardless of treatment group assignment.
Patients who are never-smokers; defined as no more than 100 cigarettes or its equivalent in his/her lifetime.

Female patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding or male or female patients of reproductive potential who are not willing to employ effective birth control from screening to 90 days after the last dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Judgment by the Investigator that the patient should not participate in the study if the patient is unlikely to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements.

criteria.text: Patient must be capable of giving signed informed consent, including mandatory genetic informed consent and compliance with ICF and protocol requirements.
Signed and dated written ICFs must be provided prior to any mandatory study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses.
Patients must provide signed and dated written optional genetic informed consent prior to collection of a sample for optional genetic analysis at the time of second screening.
ICF1 must be signed and dated prior to any study procedures and prior to the planned surgical resection of the primary NSCLC.
Age ≥18 years at the time of screening.
Male and/or female.
Diagnosis of histologically confirmed NSCLC (WHO 2015 classification) with resectable (stage II-III) disease (according to IASLC Staging Manual in Thoracic Oncology v8.0).
Select (ie, T3N2 or T4N2) stage IIIB patients will be eligible, provided that they are upstaged to T3N2 or T4N2 based on confirmed pathology.
Patients who are staged as T3N2 or T4N2 prior to surgery are not eligible.
A contrast-enhanced CT or MRI scan of the chest must have been done for surgical planning prior to surgery.
Complete resection of the primary NSCLC is mandatory.
Patients undergoing wedge resection are not eligible for this study.
Patients undergoing segmentectomy must have tumors less than 2 cm in maximum diameter.

Where a resection has been extended by means of a wedge resection of an adjacent lobe to ensure complete resection of a tumor at or crossing a fissure between lobes, this is acceptable if surgical margins are clear of disease.
Where the resection of a second tumor nodule (eg, a T4 lesion) is undertaken by means of a wedge resection of a separate lobe, then the patient is not eligible.
The surgeon performing the resection should remove all gross disease by the end of surgery.
All surgical margins of resection must be macroscopically negative for tumor.

Pathology and/or operative reports must include the examination of at least 2 different mediastinal lymph node (N2) levels, one of which is the subcarinal node-group (level 7) and the second of which is lobe-specific.
No extracapsular nodal extension of the tumor is observed in resected mediastinal N2 lymph nodes.
All patients who enrol in the study prior to surgery must have a pre-surgical plasma sample collected for MRD evaluation.
Confirmation of suitable samples of resected tumor tissue and whole blood for WES of tumor and germline DNA, respectively, and creation of Sponsor-approved personalized panel for MRD detection.
Germline sequencing of whole blood is mandatory.
If a patient's tumor has less than the requisite 50 tumor-specific variants, a panel cannot be built and the patient will no longer be able to participate in the study.
Established MRD status (MRD+ or MRD-) based on Sponsor-approved personalized assay of a plasma sample collected at Week 3-5 (Day 21-35) post-surgery.
Known tumor PD-L1 status determined at a central reference laboratory testing service using a validated Ventana SP263 PD-L1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) assay prior randomization.
Patients with unknown PD-L1 status are not eligible for the study.
Post-operative CT scan of the chest (including liver and adrenal glands) performed within 28 days + 7 days prior to randomization.
ICF2 must be signed and dated after MRD status is determined and prior to initiation of any study-specific procedures, sampling, and analyses outlined in SoAs in Table 2 and Table 3.
Randomization must occur within the 12 weeks (+ 7 days) following surgery.
WHO/Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 or 1.

Complete postoperative wound healing must have occurred prior to randomization; patients must have recovered from all acute, reversible toxic effects from prior treatments (excluding alopecia) that could potentially adversely impact further administration of durvalumab/placebo or chemotherapy according to the Investigator's judgment.
Eligible to tolerate 4 cycles of platinum-based adjuvant chemotherapy
Adequate organ and marrow function as described in the protocol.
Must have a life expectancy of at least 12 weeks
Body weight >30 kg
Post-operative imaging demonstrating unequivocal evidence of disease recurrence or tissue biopsy-proven disease recurrence.
EGFR-mutant and/or ALK-translocation-positive, as assessed either from a pre-surgical biopsy sample (preferred) or the resected tumor tissue (if biopsy was not evaluable or available).
Mixed small cell and NSCLC histology.

Require re-resection or are deemed to have unresectable NSCLC by a multidisciplinary evaluation that must include a thoracic surgeon who performs lung cancer surgery as a significant part of their practice.
Patients who are candidates to undergo only wedge resections.
History of allogeneic organ or bone marrow transplantation.
Non-leukocyte-depleted whole blood transfusion within 120 days of genetic sample collection.

Active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders (including inflammatory bowel disease [eg, colitis or Crohn's disease], diverticulitis [with the exception of diverticulosis], systemic lupus erythematosus, Sarcoidosis syndrome, or Wegener syndrome [granulomatosis with polyangiitis, Graves' disease, rheumatoid arthritis, hypophysitis, uveitis, etc]).

Uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, unstable angina pectoris, uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, active ILD, serious chronic gastrointestinal conditions associated with diarrhea, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, substantially increase risk of incurring AEs, or compromise the ability of the patient to give written informed consent.
History of another primary malignancy, except for
History of active primary immunodeficiency

Active infection, including tuberculosis (clinical evaluation that includes clinical history, physical examination, and radiographic findings, and tuberculosis testing in line with local practice), hepatitis B (HBV; known positive HBV surface antigen [HBsAg] result), hepatitis C (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus infection (positive HIV 1/2 antibodies).
Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any of the IPs or any of the IP excipients.
Any medical contraindication to treatment with platinum-based doublet chemotherapy as listed in the local labeling.
Received any prior adjuvant therapy for NSCLC or any prior exposure to durvalumab.
Any concurrent chemotherapy, IP, biologic, or hormonal therapy for cancer treatment.
Radiotherapy treatment for NSCLC in the neoadjuvant setting.
Radiotherapy treatment to more than 30% of the bone marrow or with a wide field of radiation within 4 weeks of the first dose of IP.
Receipt of live attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Major surgical procedure (as defined by the Investigator) within 28 days prior to the first dose of IP.
Current or prior use of immunosuppressive medication within 14 days before the first dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Participation in another clinical study with an IP administered since completion of surgery.
Previous IP assignment in the present study.
Concurrent enrollment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational (noninterventional) clinical study, or during the follow-up period of an interventional study.
Prior randomization or treatment in a previous durvalumab clinical study regardless of treatment group assignment.
Patients who are never-smokers; defined as no more than 100 cigarettes or its equivalent in his/her lifetime.

Female patients who are pregnant or breastfeeding or male or female patients of reproductive potential who are not willing to employ effective birth control from screening to 90 days after the last dose of durvalumab/placebo.
Judgment by the Investigator that the patient should not participate in the study if the patient is unlikely to comply with study procedures, restrictions, and requirements.

criteria.text: The prospective participant must sign the informed consent.
The patient must have a pathological or cytological diagnosis of metastatic or relapsed advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with measurable lesions according to RECIST 1.1.
The patient must have previously received at least two systemic therapies, allowing for third-line or higher chemotherapy, or be unable to tolerate chemotherapy.

The patient must have negative results for driver gene testing, or positive results who have already received relevant targeted drugs or systemic anti-tumor treatments and are either resistant or unable to tolerate them.
The patient must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0-2 and an expected survival time of ≥ 3 months.

The patient must have normal major organ function: renal function with creatinine clearance rate ≥ 60 mL/min; liver function with bilirubin ≤ 1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN), ALT/AST ≤ 2.5× ULN (for patients with documented liver metastasis, AST and ALT levels ≤ 5× ULN).

The patient must have good hematological function, defined as an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5×10^9/L, platelet count ≥ 100×10^9/L, hemoglobin ≥ 90g/L (without blood transfusion or erythropoietin [EPO] dependency within the last 7 days).

The patient must have good coagulation function, defined as an international normalized ratio (INR) or prothrombin time (PT) ≤ 1.5× ULN; if the subject is on anticoagulation therapy, PT should be within the intended therapeutic range of the anticoagulant.

Female patients of childbearing potential must agree to use contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study ends, must not be breastfeeding, and must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment. Male patients must agree to use contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study ends.
The patient must have well-controlled pleural or peritoneal effusions that do not cause grade 2 or higher respiratory syndrome (≥ CTCAE grade 2).

The patient must be without clinical symptoms of intracranial hypertension caused by brain metastases, or have brain metastasis symptoms that are stable after prior treatment (radiation therapy or surgery) of brain or meningeal metastasis (usually requiring more than 4 weeks post-radiation therapy).

The patient must not have previously failed treatment with multi-target anti-angiogenic drugs, such as anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, lenvatinib, etc. The use of bevacizumab is allowed, but the last administration must be more than 3 weeks before enrollment.
The patient must not have small cell lung cancer (including small cell carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer mixed with other types of tumors).
The patient must not be testing positive for driver genes but not treated with TKIs.

The patient must not have tumor invasion of large blood vessels, central squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with cavitation, or non-small cell lung cancer with hemoptysis (>5ml/day), or where the tumor is likely to invade important blood vessels and cause fatal bleeding during the subsequent study period.
The patient must not be accompanied by other types of malignant tumors within the past 5 years or currently.

The patient must not be planning to receive systemic anti-tumor therapy within 4 weeks before enrollment or during the study period, including cytotoxic therapy, signal transduction inhibitors, and immunotherapy (or mitomycin C within 6 weeks before receiving experimental drug therapy); received extended-field radiation therapy (EF-RT) within 4 weeks before enrollment or limited-field radiation therapy within 2 weeks before enrollment with evaluation of lesions recommended.
The patient must not have unremitting toxic reactions caused by previous treatment, CTCAE grade >1, excluding hair loss.
The patient must not have various factors affecting oral medication (such as inability to swallow, gastrointestinal resection, chronic diarrhea, bowel obstruction).
The patient must not have pleural effusion or ascites leading to respiratory syndrome (≥CTCAE grade 2).
The patient must not have symptoms of brain metastasis not controlled and treated within 2 months.
The patient must not have the presence of any severe or uncontrolled disease.
The patient must not have had major surgery, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days before enrollment.

The patient must not have a bleeding diathesis or history of significant bleeding, regardless of severity; any wound, ulcer, or fracture that has not healed following a bleeding or bleeding event (≥CTCAE grade 3).
The patient must not have had arterial/venous thrombosis within 6 months, such as cerebrovascular accident (including transient ischemic attack), venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism.
The patient must not have a history of substance abuse that cannot be quit or diagnosed with psychiatric disorders.
The patient must not have participated in other clinical trials of anti-tumor drugs within 4 weeks.
The patient must not be diagnosed with diseases that severely jeopardize patient safety or affect the completion of this study.

The patient must not have a known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (i.e., HIV 1/2 antibody positive); untreated active hepatitis B; active HCV infection (HCV antibody positive and HCV-RNA levels above detection limit).

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello, and thank you for your interest in the study "Efficacy and Safety of Vorolanib Monotherapy As Third-line or Later Treatment for Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer Patients: a Single-arm, Prospective, Open-label Phase II Clinical Study". I'll ask you a short series of questions, one at a time. You can skip any question. A study coordinator will review everything you tell me and follow up with you.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you willing to sign an informed consent form to participate in this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I would sign the informed consent form.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you already signed the informed consent form?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Not yet, that's what I'm agreeing to do now. I haven't put pen to paper on it just yet.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received a diagnosis of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread or returned, with tumors that can be measured on scans?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yeah, the biopsy confirmed it was advanced non-small cell lung cancer. It came back and has spread around now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do your recent scans show tumors that can be measured to track their size?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the exact details of the scans. I know the cancer is there and has spread, but I don't keep track of the measurements.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you previously received at least two different systemic cancer treatments (such as chemotherapy or targeted therapy)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have had a few treatments over the years. I lose track of how many.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us count, can you list the types of treatments you've had, such as chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy? We need to know if you've had at least two different ones.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I've had a mix of things over the years, mostly chemo and some targeted pills, but I really can't list them all out or remember exactly which was which.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a test to check for specific gene changes in your cancer (driver gene testing), and if so, were the results positive or negative?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't keep track of specific gene test results or what they were called.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. On a scale of 0 to 2, how would you rate your ability to carry out normal daily activities? (0 = fully active, 1 = restricted but ambulatory, 2 = in bed <50% of day). Also, has your doctor estimated you have at least 3 months left to live?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I get tired pretty easily and I rest most afternoons, so I'd say I'm restricted but still walking around. As for how long I have left, my doctor hasn't given me a specific timeline like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Based on what you shared, it sounds like your ECOG score is 1 (restricted but ambulatory). Does that match how you're feeling?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yeah, that sounds about right. I'm still on my feet, just need to take it easy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently breastfeeding? Also, are you able to use effective contraception during the study and for 6 months after it ends?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: That one is for female patients. I am a man.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have fluid buildup in your chest or abdomen that is causing moderate breathing problems or other significant symptoms?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any fluid buildup causing trouble. I'm just tired.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with brain metastases? If so, are your symptoms currently stable after prior treatment like radiation or surgery?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I haven't heard anything about my cancer spreading to my brain.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever received treatment with anti-angiogenic drugs like anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, or lenvatinib? (Note: Bevacizumab is allowed, but if you had it, it must have been more than 3 weeks ago.)

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I have taken so many pills, maybe one of those, I could not say.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To help us check, could you list the exact names of the pills you've taken? Or, if you aren't sure, is it possible you took any of these: anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, or lenvatinib?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I really can't remember the exact names of the pills. I've taken so many over the years, I just know I've had a lot of treatments, but I can't say for sure if I took those specific ones.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had genetic testing for 'driver genes' in your cancer? If yes, did you receive treatment with targeted pills called TKIs?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't keep track of specific gene test results or what they were called.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been told you have bleeding from the lungs (hemoptysis) of more than 5ml per day, or that your tumor is close to large blood vessels or has cavitation?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No hemoptysis. I do not cough up any blood.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you been diagnosed with any other types of cancer in the last 5 years, or do you have any other cancer diagnosis right now?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been diagnosed with any other cancers. Just the lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you planning to start any new cancer treatments (like chemo, immunotherapy, or targeted pills) in the next 4 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I am not planning any other anti-tumor treatment.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any ongoing side effects from your previous cancer treatments that are moderate or severe (grade >1), excluding hair loss?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't really keep track of side effects like that. I just know I get tired and need to rest.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To make sure you can take the study medication by mouth, do you have any trouble swallowing, or have you had stomach or bowel surgery, chronic diarrhea, or a bowel obstruction?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have any trouble swallowing. I haven't had stomach or bowel surgery, and I'm not dealing with chronic diarrhea or any blockages.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any symptoms of brain metastasis (like headaches, vision changes, or balance issues) that were not controlled or treated within the last 2 months? If you aren't sure, that's okay to say.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any of those symptoms like headaches or balance issues. I don't know about brain metastases, but I haven't noticed anything like that.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you currently have any severe or uncontrolled health conditions, other than the cancer being studied?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I haven't had any other major health issues besides the lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, do you have any other serious health conditions (like heart, kidney, or liver disease) that are currently uncontrolled or not well-managed with medication?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I haven't had any other major health issues besides the lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any major surgery, an open biopsy, or a significant traumatic injury in the last 28 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No surgery, no biopsy and no injuries in the last two months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a condition that makes it hard for your blood to clot, or any history of significant bleeding (like heavy nosebleeds or bleeding in the stomach)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I haven't had any history of bleeding problems or clotting issues.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever had a blood clot in your veins or lungs, or a stroke or TIA (mini-stroke) in the last 6 months? It's okay if you aren't sure.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I haven't had any history of blood clots or strokes.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder, or had trouble quitting substance use (like alcohol or drugs) in the past?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I like a drink, but I could quit if I had to. I don't have any trouble quitting substances.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you taken part in any other clinical trials for cancer drugs in the last 4 weeks?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I have not been in any other clinical trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any other serious health conditions that might make it unsafe to take part in this study or prevent you from completing it?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know about that. I haven't had any other major health issues besides the lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with HIV, or had active Hepatitis B or C?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I do not have HIV. I haven't heard anything about having Hepatitis B or C either.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with active Hepatitis B or C, or told you have untreated Hepatitis B?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't been told I have Hepatitis B or C. I don't know about any untreated Hepatitis B.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. A study coordinator will review your answers and contact you about next steps.

criteria.text: The prospective participant must sign the informed consent.
The patient must have a pathological or cytological diagnosis of metastatic or relapsed advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with measurable lesions according to RECIST 1.1.
The patient must have previously received at least two systemic therapies, allowing for third-line or higher chemotherapy, or be unable to tolerate chemotherapy.

The patient must have negative results for driver gene testing, or positive results who have already received relevant targeted drugs or systemic anti-tumor treatments and are either resistant or unable to tolerate them.
The patient must have an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score of 0-2 and an expected survival time of ≥ 3 months.

The patient must have normal major organ function: renal function with creatinine clearance rate ≥ 60 mL/min; liver function with bilirubin ≤ 1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN), ALT/AST ≤ 2.5× ULN (for patients with documented liver metastasis, AST and ALT levels ≤ 5× ULN).

The patient must have good hematological function, defined as an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5×10^9/L, platelet count ≥ 100×10^9/L, hemoglobin ≥ 90g/L (without blood transfusion or erythropoietin [EPO] dependency within the last 7 days).

The patient must have good coagulation function, defined as an international normalized ratio (INR) or prothrombin time (PT) ≤ 1.5× ULN; if the subject is on anticoagulation therapy, PT should be within the intended therapeutic range of the anticoagulant.

Female patients of childbearing potential must agree to use contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study ends, must not be breastfeeding, and must have a negative serum or urine pregnancy test within 7 days before enrollment. Male patients must agree to use contraception during the study and for 6 months after the study ends.
The patient must have well-controlled pleural or peritoneal effusions that do not cause grade 2 or higher respiratory syndrome (≥ CTCAE grade 2).

The patient must be without clinical symptoms of intracranial hypertension caused by brain metastases, or have brain metastasis symptoms that are stable after prior treatment (radiation therapy or surgery) of brain or meningeal metastasis (usually requiring more than 4 weeks post-radiation therapy).

The patient must not have previously failed treatment with multi-target anti-angiogenic drugs, such as anlotinib, cabozantinib, apatinib, lenvatinib, etc. The use of bevacizumab is allowed, but the last administration must be more than 3 weeks before enrollment.
The patient must not have small cell lung cancer (including small cell carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer mixed with other types of tumors).
The patient must not be testing positive for driver genes but not treated with TKIs.

The patient must not have tumor invasion of large blood vessels, central squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with cavitation, or non-small cell lung cancer with hemoptysis (>5ml/day), or where the tumor is likely to invade important blood vessels and cause fatal bleeding during the subsequent study period.
The patient must not be accompanied by other types of malignant tumors within the past 5 years or currently.

The patient must not be planning to receive systemic anti-tumor therapy within 4 weeks before enrollment or during the study period, including cytotoxic therapy, signal transduction inhibitors, and immunotherapy (or mitomycin C within 6 weeks before receiving experimental drug therapy); received extended-field radiation therapy (EF-RT) within 4 weeks before enrollment or limited-field radiation therapy within 2 weeks before enrollment with evaluation of lesions recommended.
The patient must not have unremitting toxic reactions caused by previous treatment, CTCAE grade >1, excluding hair loss.
The patient must not have various factors affecting oral medication (such as inability to swallow, gastrointestinal resection, chronic diarrhea, bowel obstruction).
The patient must not have pleural effusion or ascites leading to respiratory syndrome (≥CTCAE grade 2).
The patient must not have symptoms of brain metastasis not controlled and treated within 2 months.
The patient must not have the presence of any severe or uncontrolled disease.
The patient must not have had major surgery, open biopsy, or significant traumatic injury within 28 days before enrollment.

The patient must not have a bleeding diathesis or history of significant bleeding, regardless of severity; any wound, ulcer, or fracture that has not healed following a bleeding or bleeding event (≥CTCAE grade 3).
The patient must not have had arterial/venous thrombosis within 6 months, such as cerebrovascular accident (including transient ischemic attack), venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism.
The patient must not have a history of substance abuse that cannot be quit or diagnosed with psychiatric disorders.
The patient must not have participated in other clinical trials of anti-tumor drugs within 4 weeks.
The patient must not be diagnosed with diseases that severely jeopardize patient safety or affect the completion of this study.

The patient must not have a known history of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection (i.e., HIV 1/2 antibody positive); untreated active hepatitis B; active HCV infection (HCV antibody positive and HCV-RNA levels above detection limit).
